tokyo_kibun_zushi.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Tax-included (the shop's own card is headed 税込価格). Two independent shop-sourced lists agree: the shop-maintained HotPepper page strJ000126526 (最終更新日 2026/01/05 — HotPepper listings are maintained by the shop, so this counts as authoritative) and a 2026/05 photograph of the laminated お品書き and お飲み物 cards that sit on the counter. Address checked against both — 東京都台東区浅草1-17-10 on HotPepper and on Tabelog, the same shop. PRICES HAVE MOVED RECENTLY, and dating the photos proves it: the 2025/11 and 2025/12 cards read 上寿司 七種 ¥4,000 / おすすめ寿司 十一種 ¥8,250, while the 2026/02 and 2026/05 cards read ¥4,400 and ¥8,800; the drinks card rose from 菊正宗 ¥800 and キリンラガー ¥800 to ¥850 each and 麦焼酎 神の河 from ¥650 to ¥700. The figures below are the current (2026) ones and are corroborated by dated 2026/06 and 2026/07 Tabelog reviews quoting ¥4,400 for 上寿司 and ¥8,800 for おまかせ. Founded 1903; 寿司 百名店 TOKYO 2025. The counter has NO allergen information of any kind — no chart, no notice, no English menu — so every gluten judgement below is reasoned from the shop's own dish descriptions and dated first-hand reports, not from a declaration. Several items (巻物, 煮魚, 焼魚, 椀物, 酢物, おつまみ) are listed by the shop with no price at all: 「ご希望に合わせてご用意いたします」, i.e. made to order, ask. No price is invented for them here. Closed Wednesdays; 12:00-14:00 / 17:00-21:00 (Sun & holidays 12:00-19:00).

items.en: 'Upper' nigiri set — the everyday order and the reason most people come. The shop's own HotPepper copy: にぎり寿司のセット。内容は、季節によって変動します (a set of nigiri; the contents change with the season). The shop's 2025 card specified 七種 (seven kinds); the 2026 card drops the count
items.note: Raw fish on vinegared rice looks gluten-free and is not. This is a straight Edomae counter: a 2026/07 diner describes the house technique as 「〆方やツメ、シャリの具合」— ツメ is the sweet reduced soy-and-mirin glaze brushed onto the cooked toppings, and Japanese soy sauce is brewed with wheat by default. The shop's own copy for its 煮はまぐり (which appears in the sets) says 濃厚なタレ — a rich soy tare. Add the counter soy sauce you dip with, and the sushi vinegar in the shari, on which the shop publishes nothing. There is no allergen chart and no gluten-free tamari here. Fish and shellfish, so not vegan either.

items.en: The chef's recommended nigiri course — the big order, and what regulars call おまかせ. The shop's 2025 card specified 十一種 (eleven kinds); the 2026 card drops the count. A 2026/07 diner's seating ran ひらめ (flounder), すみいか (golden cuttlefish), マグロ (tuna), こはだ (gizzard shad), あかがい (ark shell), くるまえび (kuruma prawn), はまぐり (clam), うに (sea urchin) and あなご (conger eel)
items.note: The 2026/07 line-up quoted above is one seating and rotates, but two of the pieces named are the classic glazed ones: 煮はまぐり and 穴子 both carry ツメ, the soy-and-mirin glaze the shop is praised for, and そのタレ is wheat soy sauce unless a tamari is named — it is not. こはだ is cured in salt and vinegar rather than soy, but it reaches you on shari of undeclared seasoning at a counter where wheat soy is in constant use. No allergen information is published. Not vegan.

items.en: Chirashi — the day's sliced fish spread over a bowl of sushi rice rather than pressed into nigiri. Same kitchen, same fish, cheaper than the nigiri course
items.note: Same reasoning as the nigiri: the shop composes it from the Edomae toppings (which include the ツメ-glazed cooked pieces) and you season it at the table with the counter soy sauce, which is wheat-brewed by default. The shop makes no ingredient statement about the sushi vinegar. Fish, so not vegan.

items.en: Tekka-don — sliced tuna over rice. The most expensive of the rice bowls here, and the simplest
items.note: The bowl closest to being wheat-free on this menu — tuna and rice — but it is eaten with soy sauce, and the shop publishes nothing about whether the fish is served plain or 漬け (marinated in soy). Wheat soy sauce is the Japanese default and there is no tamari here, so treat it as wheat. Tuna, so not vegan.

items.en: Simmered hamaguri clam — a house speciality. The shop's own words: 人気の煮はまぐり。濃厚なタレと煮はまぐりの相性抜群。このはまぐりを召し上がりに訪れるお客様も多数いるほど (people come for this clam alone). Sold as a nigiri topping and as a drinking snack
items.note: The shop itself names the 濃厚なタレ — a rich simmering tare. A Japanese ni-tsume tare is soy sauce, mirin and sugar reduced down, and Japanese soy sauce contains wheat unless a gluten-free tamari is specified. Nothing here specifies one. This is the single clearest wheat item on the food menu. Shellfish, so not vegan. Price is given by the shop as 1,000円〜 — it moves with the size of the clam.

items.en: House-made dried fish. The shop's own copy: 名物は、自家製の干物。大振りの干物と共に、日本酒を — a big piece of himono is the thing to drink sake with here
items.note: Genuinely worth asking about rather than writing off. A plain 干物 is fish, salt and air — no wheat at all — and this is the one item on the menu that could be clear. But みりん干し and 醤油干し are common variants that are cured in soy sauce, and the shop says only 自家製 with no description of the cure. Ask which. Priced 時価 (market price), so no figure is recorded here. Fish, not vegan.

items.en: Rolled sushi, various — made to order rather than from a fixed list. The shop's note reads 巻物各種…ご希望に合わせてご用意いたします (we will prepare them to your wish)
items.note: No fillings and no prices are published, so nothing specific can be stated — but every common Edomae maki routes through wheat: 干瓢巻 is gourd simmered in soy sauce, 鉄火巻 and 河童巻 are dipped in it, and 玉子 is normally seasoned. Treat as wheat unless you can get a specific answer at the counter. 'Ask' on vegan only because a plain 河童巻 (cucumber) would be plant-based if the rice seasoning and the dipping soy were resolved — the shop names no such roll, so do not assume it exists. No price is published for these; none is invented here.

items.en: Clear soup. The shop specifies はまぐり・魚等 — clam or fish
items.note: Named by the shop as clam or fish based, so not vegan, full stop. It is also a gluten question and the same answer: a Japanese clear soup is seasoned with 薄口醤油 or 白だし, both soy-sauce products and both wheat-brewed by default. Priced 時価; no figure is recorded.

items.en: Miso soup. The shop specifies はまぐり・魚等 — clam or fish
items.note: Two separate gluten routes and neither is declared: the dashi (a Japanese kitchen almost never builds it from katsuobushi and water alone — it reaches for 白だし or だし醤油, which are soy sauce) and the miso itself, which can be 麦味噌, i.e. barley. Barley is not on Japan's statutory allergen list, so it would not have to be declared even if the shop labelled anything, and it does not. Clam or fish based, so not vegan. 時価.

items.en: Simmered fish — made to order from whatever is in the case. Listed by the shop under 「ご希望に合わせてご用意いたします」
items.note: 煮魚 means fish simmered in a soy-sauce, mirin, sake and sugar liquor — the technique is defined by the soy sauce, which is wheat-brewed by default and is not stated to be a gluten-free tamari here. Fish, not vegan. No price is published.

items.en: Grilled fish — made to order. Listed by the shop under 「ご希望に合わせてご用意いたします」
items.note: Worth asking rather than assuming. 塩焼き — salt-grilled — carries no wheat; 照り焼き and 幽庵焼き are glazed in soy sauce and do. The shop states neither, so the question to put at the counter is 塩焼きですか、タレですか. Fish, not vegan. No price is published.

items.en: Vinegared side dish — made to order. Listed by the shop under 「ご希望に合わせてご用意いたします」
items.note: Nothing is described, so nothing can be asserted. The thing to check is the dressing: 二杯酢 and 三杯酢 both contain soy sauce (wheat) while a plain 甘酢 does not, and most sunomono at a sushi counter contain seafood and are finished with dashi. No price is published.

items.en: Drinking snacks — assembled from the day's fish at the chef's discretion. A 2026/07 diner was served 平目 (flounder), タコ (octopus) and 貝 (shellfish) as tsumami alongside the 上寿司
items.note: The example above is one visit's plate, not a fixed dish. Plain sliced sashimi carries no wheat in itself — the wheat arrives with the soy sauce you dip it in, and with any 煮 or タレ preparation such as this shop's 煮はまぐり. Ask for it plain and skip the soy. Fish and shellfish, so not vegan. No price is published.

items.en: Kiku-Masamune — the Nada dry sake that is the benchmark of old-Tokyo sushi counters. The house pour
items.note: Sake is brewed from rice, rice koji and water — no wheat, no barley, no malt. The grade is not stated on the card; even a honjozo grade adds distilled alcohol, not a gluten grain. Vegan: no animal products in sake, and this shop's list carries no nigori or fined-with-gelatin oddity. Was ¥800 on the 2025/11 card, ¥850 on the 2026/05 card.

items.en: Shimeharitsuru — a clean, quiet Niigata sake from Miyao Shuzo
items.note: Rice, rice koji and water. No gluten grain in sake. Vegan.

items.en: Kiyoizumi, tokubetsu junmai grade — Niigata
items.note: 純米 means the only ingredients permitted are rice, rice koji and water — no added alcohol and, crucially here, no gluten grain of any kind. Vegan.

items.en: Suigei ('drunken whale'), tokubetsu junmai — the dry Kochi sake made to be drunk with fish
items.note: 純米 grade: rice, rice koji and water only. No wheat or barley. Vegan.

items.note: An aged (熟成) sake — the ageing is in tank, not in a barrel of another grain's spirit. Rice, rice koji and water. No gluten grain. Vegan. Was ¥1,100 on the 2025/11 card.

items.en: Isojiman, junmai ginjo — the Shizuoka sake famous for being poured at the 2008 G8 summit. The most expensive bottle on the list
items.note: 純米吟醸: rice, rice koji, water, nothing else. No gluten grain. Vegan. On the shop's HotPepper list and on the 2025/11 counter card, but dropped from the 2026/05 card — ask whether it is still open.

READ THIS FIRST: the site's own footer states 「※実店舗はございません。通販をご利用ください。」 — there is NO walk-in shop at the Matsugaya address; it is a workshop and mail-order only, with phone ordering 10:00–18:00, closed Wed and Sun. Items marked 【冷凍】 ship frozen. The shop's materials page states: 「小麦・乳製品・卵を使用せず、代わりに米粉などのグルテンを含まない粉類や、植物性の素材だけを使っています。また、植物性・グルテンフリー専門の工房ですので、これらの原料の工房への持ち込みもなく、コンタミネーションの心配はございません。」 — a dedicated plant-based and gluten-free workshop with no wheat, dairy or egg brought onto the premises. That is a FACILITY-level claim, not just a product one, and every product page carries its own 特定原材料（28品目中） line — none of the ones checked names 小麦. Sweeteners are てんさい糖 / メープルシロップ / 米飴, i.e. no honey. Product names have had a trailing SKU artefact ("_n", "_") trimmed; 「紙袋付き / 紙袋なし」 marks the with- or without-gift-bag variant of the same tin.

tokyo_tsukushi.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Tax-included. Taken from the shop's own Gurunavi オフィシャルページ (r.gnavi.co.jp/b843100, address confirmed as 台東区浅草2-4-13 on Hoppy-dōri) and cross-checked against the 公式 Tabelog menu, 更新日 2025/04/03 — the two agree line for line. Note the shop's own footnote: this printed list is a selection only. It states it also stocks もんじゃ 38 kinds, お好み焼き 40 kinds, 鉄板焼き 35 kinds, 焼きそば・焼きうどん 10 kinds and 一品料理 36 kinds, so the board in front of you is far longer than what either site publishes. Open since 1967. The shop's `website` field points at b843100.gorp.jp, which now returns a Gnavi CAPTCHA page; r.gnavi.co.jp/b843100/ is the same content and answers cleanly.

items.en: The house monjayaki — takuan pickle, fish sausage, chikuwa and squid. The shop's premium bowl and its oddest
items.note: もんじゃ焼き＝小麦粉と出汁を溶いた生地. Monja batter is wheat flour slaked with dashi, cooked on a griddle shared with okonomiyaki and yakisoba — wheat by definition and by contact. Fish sausage and chikuwa are surimi; the dashi is bonito.

items.en: Gomoku monjayaki — dried squid strips, sakura shrimp and squid. Unchanged for fifty years, per the shop
items.note: Wheat-flour monja batter and a shared griddle. Shrimp and squid.

items.en: Mixed monjayaki — minced pork, shrimp and squid, the standard three. Adding pork belly and egg makes it デラックスもんじゃ
items.note: Wheat batter. The Gurunavi page notes デラックスもんじゃ at ¥972 as an add-on version, which is below the base price and looks like an un-updated figure — ask at the counter.

items.ja: カレーコンビーフもんじゃ
items.en: Curry and corned-beef monjayaki — deliberately Showa-era nostalgia
items.note: Wheat batter plus Japanese curry powder/roux, which is itself normally wheat-thickened.

items.en: Seafood monjayaki — squid, shrimp, scallop and oyster
items.note: Wheat batter; shellfish throughout.

items.ja: 明太もちチーズもんじゃ
items.en: Mentaiko, mochi and cheese monjayaki — the shop's own number-one seller
items.note: Wheat batter. Mentaiko is cured in a marinade that normally contains soy sauce and mirin, i.e. more wheat, plus dairy cheese.

items.en: 'GACKT' monjayaki — beef tendon, spring onion, kimchi and Korean chilli. Named after the singer, who ate it here
items.note: Wheat batter; kimchi is normally made with fish sauce or salted shrimp.

items.ja: ももクロ もんじゃ
items.en: 'Momoiro Clover Z' monjayaki — natto, kimchi and spring onion
items.note: Wheat batter. Natto's sachet tare is soy-sauce based (wheat); kimchi usually carries fish sauce.

items.en: Deluxe okonomiyaki — pork, squid, minced meat and shrimp under a soft-set egg
items.note: お好み焼き＝小麦粉生地. Wheat batter, wheat-thickened okonomi sauce, egg.

items.en: 'Popeye' okonomiyaki — spinach and cheese in a thinly-spread batter, finished with soft-set egg
items.note: Wheat batter, egg, dairy cheese.

items.en: Tonpeiyaki — pork belly on a thin batter crêpe with soft-set egg
items.note: Wheat crêpe batter, egg, and the sauce is wheat-thickened okonomi sauce.

items.en: Korean chijimi pancake — choice of garlic-chive, potato or kimchi
items.note: Chijimi batter is wheat flour (usually with some potato starch) and egg; the dipping sauce is soy-based. Kimchi version also carries fish sauce.

items.en: 'Strongest' yakisoba — thick noodles ordered in from a Kyoto noodle-maker
items.section: 焼きそば・焼きうどん Yakisoba & yaki-udon
items.note: 焼きそば麺＝小麦. Yakisoba noodles are wheat, and yakisoba sauce is a wheat-thickened Worcestershire style.

items.en: Gomoku yakisoba — pork and seafood, a big plate
items.section: 焼きそば・焼きうどん Yakisoba & yaki-udon
items.note: Wheat noodles, wheat-thickened sauce, seafood.

items.en: Yaki-udon, finished with the house sauce
items.section: 焼きそば・焼きうどん Yakisoba & yaki-udon
items.note: うどん＝小麦. Udon is wheat, and the finish is sauce.

items.en: Griddled pork offal — the shop's self-declared number-one snack
items.note: Horumon tare is soy-sauce and miso based, i.e. wheat, and it is cooked on the same griddle as the wheat-batter dishes.

items.en: Simmered beef tendon — the shop calls it the thing to order first on Hoppy Street
items.note: Beef tendon simmered in soy sauce and mirin — wheat by default in Japan unless a gluten-free tamari is named, and it is not.

items.en: Griddled onion in butter with the owner's own tare
items.note: Dairy butter, so not vegan. The 'ママが作った絶品のタレ' is unspecified — a house tare in an izakaya is soy-sauce based unless told otherwise, and the griddle is shared with wheat batter, so ask before assuming.

items.en: Squid tentacles stir-fried with kimchi in the house tare
items.note: House tare (soy-based) plus kimchi, which normally carries fish sauce or salted shrimp; squid.

items.en: Blanched cabbage with the owner's own blended miso
items.note: Just cabbage and miso, so the closest thing to a plant dish here — but a blended Japanese miso may be 麦味噌 (barley miso, a gluten grain that is NOT on Japan's statutory allergen list), and household miso dips routinely carry dashi or mirin. Ask what is in the blend.

items.en: Draught beer, medium or small glass. A 一口生 taster size is also poured
items.note: Beer is brewed from barley malt — never gluten-free. Fining agents mean vegan status varies by brand.

items.en: Bottled beer, medium bottle — Kirin Lager or Asahi Super Dry
items.note: Barley malt — not gluten-free. Both Kirin Lager and Asahi Super Dry are malt-and-rice lagers with no animal ingredient.

items.ja: 各種 サワー（酎ハイ）
items.en: Shochu highballs (sour), various flavours
items.note: The base shochu may be 麦焼酎 (barley) — the shop's bottle-keep list explicitly offers 麦 — so ask for an imo (sweet-potato) base if gluten matters.

items.en: Fresh grape sour
items.note: Shochu base unspecified; barley shochu is on this shop's list, so ask.

items.en: Shochu highball with a pickled plum
items.note: Same question as the other sours — the shochu base may be barley.

items.en: Hoppy, white or black — the low-alcohol malt mixer Asakusa's Hoppy Street is named for, served with shochu
items.note: Hoppy is brewed from barley malt and hops. Not gluten-free, despite being nearly alcohol-free on its own.

items.ja: ハイボール サントリー角
items.en: Suntory Kakubin whisky highball
items.note: Blended Japanese whisky is distilled from malted barley. Distillation removes most gluten protein but this app does not flag malt drinks gluten-free.

items.en: House-made plum wine, on the rocks or with soda — the owner's recommendation
items.note: Umeshu is plums and rock sugar steeped in a spirit — commonly white liquor, but sometimes 麦焼酎 (barley). Home-made versions occasionally use honey. Ask.

items.en: Denki Bran — the 1880s Asakusa brandy-based liqueur, drunk here as the local ritual
items.note: A blend of brandy, gin, wine, curaçao and herbs whose full composition the maker does not publish; grain spirit cannot be ruled out. Ask, or skip if strict.

items.ja: 焼酎 ボトルキープ（麦・芋・ジンロ）
items.en: Bottle-keep shochu — barley, sweet potato or Jinro
items.note: 麦 is barley. The 芋 (sweet-potato) bottle is the one to take if gluten matters; Jinro is a Korean soju usually made from tapioca/rice but the recipe varies.

items.ja: フレッシュジュース（グレープフルーツ生搾り）
items.en: Fresh-squeezed grapefruit juice
items.note: Squeezed fruit and nothing else — no wheat, no barley, no animal ingredient.

items.ja: 各種 ジュース類（全11種類）
items.en: Soft drinks, eleven kinds
items.note: The eleven are not itemised on either of the shop's pages, so the individual drinks are not assessed here.

items.ja: ウーロン茶・冷やし緑茶
items.en: Oolong tea or chilled green tea
items.note: Oolong and green tea are tea leaf and water — no grain. Note this is NOT 麦茶, which is barley and would not be gluten-free.

items.ja: やきとり盛合せ 10本盛合せ
items.en: Yakitori assortment, ten skewers
items.note: An assortment arrives tare-glazed unless you ask for 塩. 焼き鳥のタレ＝醤油・みりんベース, and Japanese soy sauce is brewed with wheat by default. Even ordered 塩, the skewers are grilled over the same fire and brushed area as tare skewers.

items.ja: やきとり盛合せ 5本盛合せ
items.en: Yakitori assortment, five skewers

items.en: Three skewers buried under a heap of spring onion
items.note: Chicken skewers with a soy-based tare or a negi dressing; wheat by default.

items.en: Three skewers with spring onion and natto
items.note: Chicken, plus natto — whose sachet tare is soy-sauce based (wheat) and often contains bonito extract.

items.en: Chicken thigh skewer. Choose salt or tare, and choose how many
items.note: The cheapest skewer on the board — this is the '80 yen' of the shop's name, ¥88 with tax. たれ is soy-sauce based, so wheat; 塩 is the safer order but the same grill carries tare skewers.

items.en: Chicken and spring onion skewer
items.note: Salt or tare; the tare is wheat soy sauce and drips onto the shared grill.

items.en: Chicken neck skewer
items.note: Salt or tare; tare is wheat soy sauce.

items.en: Chicken skin skewer
items.note: Usually served tare-glazed; soy sauce is wheat.

items.en: Chicken tenderloin skewer
items.note: Salt or tare; tare is wheat soy sauce. Sasami is often finished with wasabi or plum paste, which carry their own seasonings.

items.en: Chicken tail (parson's nose) skewer
items.note: Salt or tare; tare is wheat soy sauce.

items.en: Chicken breast-bone cartilage skewer
items.note: Salt or tare; tare is wheat soy sauce.

items.en: Chicken heart skewer
items.note: Salt or tare; tare is wheat soy sauce.

items.en: Chicken aorta skewer — limited number each night
items.note: Salt or tare; tare is wheat soy sauce.

items.en: Ultra-fresh pale chicken liver skewer
items.note: Liver skewers are almost always tare-glazed — wheat soy sauce.

items.en: Chicken gizzard skewer
items.note: Salt or tare; tare is wheat soy sauce.

items.en: Minced chicken meatball skewer
items.note: Tsukune is bound with egg and, very commonly, panko or flour, then glazed with soy tare — the worst of the skewers for a coeliac.

items.en: Chicken wing
items.note: Salt or tare; tare is wheat soy sauce.

items.en: Pork belly skewer
items.note: Salt or tare; tare is wheat soy sauce.

items.en: Beef short-rib skewer
items.note: Karubi is normally marinated in a soy-sauce, mirin and sesame tare — wheat.

items.en: Grilled onion skewer
items.note: Onion alone is a plant food, but on a yakitori grill it is brushed with the same tare as the chicken (wheat soy sauce) unless you order 塩, and it cooks over dripping chicken fat. Ask for 塩 and ask about the grill.

items.en: Grilled leek skewer
items.note: Same as the onion: plant food, but tare and shared grill unless you specify 塩.

items.en: Grilled mountain yam skewer
items.note: Yam is plant food; the tare and the shared grill are the questions. やまいも is itself a listed allergen in Japan.

items.en: Grilled king oyster mushroom skewer
items.note: Mushroom is plant food; ask for 塩 and ask whether it shares the tare brush and grill with chicken.

items.en: Grilled shiitake skewer
items.note: Same as the eringi — the mushroom is fine, the tare and the grill are not established.

items.en: Grilled quail-egg skewer
items.note: Egg, so not vegan despite sitting under the vegetable heading. Usually tare-glazed.

items.en: Grilled ginkgo nut skewer
items.note: Ginkgo nuts are usually just salted, which would make this the plainest thing on the skewer list — but confirm the salt-only preparation and the shared grill.

items.ja: 三代目 もつ煮込み
items.en: 'Third-generation' simmered pork offal — the house dish since the shop opened, reworked
items.section: 三代目 信長の煮込み Simmered offal
items.note: Motsu-nikomi is simmered in miso and/or soy sauce. Both are wheat questions: soy sauce is wheat-brewed by default and the miso may be 麦味噌 (barley).

items.en: Garlic chives scrambled with egg on the hotplate
items.note: Egg. The seasoning is not stated; a griddle dish in an izakaya is normally finished with soy sauce or an oyster/soy sauce, so ask.

items.en: Spring onion, egg and natto on the hotplate
items.note: Egg plus natto — the natto tare is soy-sauce based (wheat) and generally carries bonito extract.

items.en: Nobunaga's tonpeiyaki — pork and egg on the hotplate
items.note: Tonpeiyaki is wrapped in a thin wheat-batter crêpe or egg sheet and finished with okonomi sauce and mayonnaise — wheat and egg.

items.en: Tomato baked with cheese on the hotplate
items.note: Dairy cheese. Wheat status depends on the seasoning and whether the same hotplate cooks the tonpeiyaki batter — ask.

items.en: Mountain yam baked with cheese on the hotplate
items.note: Dairy cheese; grated yam dishes are usually loosened with dashi or mentsuyu, which is soy sauce, i.e. wheat. Ask.

items.en: Fried chicken finished nanban-style on the hotplate — sweet-vinegar sauce and tartare
items.note: 唐揚げ＝小麦粉／片栗粉の衣 plus a nanban sauce built on soy sauce and vinegar, plus egg mayonnaise. Wheat, egg, and a shared fryer.

items.en: House potato salad (add a soft-boiled egg for ¥100)
items.note: Japanese potato salad is bound with egg mayonnaise, and often carries ham. Kewpie-style mayonnaise uses rice/apple vinegar rather than malt, but the ham and any seasoning are unverified — ask.

items.en: Tofu salad with sesame dressing
items.note: Commercial 胡麻ドレッシング is built on soy sauce (wheat) and normally contains egg yolk; Japanese tofu salads are also usually topped with bonito flakes.

items.en: Caesar salad with a soft-poached egg
items.note: Caesar dressing is egg, parmesan and anchovy, and the salad is normally scattered with wheat croutons.

items.ja: 信長特製 キャベツ盛り
items.en: Nobunaga's cabbage plate — with salted kombu and the house chilli miso (heat ★★)
items.note: Raw cabbage with 塩昆布 and a 自家製辛味噌. The kombu seasoning is normally soy-based, and the chilli miso may be 麦味噌 (barley) — both gluten questions, and a chilli miso often carries dashi. Ask for the cabbage plain if you want the safest version.

items.en: Thick-cut crumbed ham cutlet, one slice
items.note: カツ＝パン粉衣. Panko crumb is wheat bread, plus flour and egg in the coating, in a shared fryer.

items.en: Cheese-filled spring rolls
items.note: 春巻きの皮＝小麦. Spring-roll wrappers are wheat, plus dairy cheese.

items.en: Deep-fried chicken cartilage
items.note: Dusted and fried; even a potato-starch dusting goes into the same oil as the panko cutlets and spring rolls.

items.en: Deep-fried takoyaki
items.note: たこ焼き＝小麦粉生地. Wheat batter, wheat-thickened sauce, egg mayonnaise, bonito flakes, shared fryer.

items.ja: 新潟名物 栃尾揚げ
items.en: Tochio abura-age — Niigata's giant deep-fried tofu slab, re-grilled
items.note: The tofu slab itself is soy and oil, but it is served with a soy-sauce and spring-onion or miso topping, sometimes with bonito flakes, and it goes through the shared fryer. Ask about both the topping and the oil.

items.ja: 昔懐かし赤ウィンナー
items.en: Nostalgic red mini sausages
items.note: Pork sausage. Japanese sausage fillers often include wheat protein, and this is cooked in the shared fryer.

items.en: Fried potato-and-cheese mochi
items.note: Dairy cheese; the shared fryer carries panko and spring-roll wrapper.

items.ja: カニクリームコロッケ
items.en: Crab cream croquettes
items.note: A cream croquette is a wheat-flour béchamel in a panko crumb — wheat twice over, plus dairy and crab.

items.en: Deep-fried octopus
items.note: 唐揚げ is dusted in flour or potato starch after a soy-sauce marinade, and fried in the shared oil.

items.ja: 鶏白レバーの低温調理刺し
items.romaji: tori shiro liver teion chori sashi
items.en: Low-temperature-cooked pale chicken liver, served as sashimi — the shop's signature
items.note: Liver sashimi is eaten with soy sauce, sesame oil and salt — the soy sauce is wheat.

items.en: Cold tofu
items.note: Chilled tofu comes with soy sauce (wheat) and is nearly always topped with bonito flakes. Ask for it with nothing on it and no soy and you are down to plain tofu and ginger.

items.en: Seared edamame
items.note: Edamame and salt would be plant food and grain-free, but 炙り means these go over the yakitori grill where tare drips, and a seared version is often brushed with something. Ask.

items.en: Mountain yam cut into batons
items.note: Served with soy sauce and nori, and usually a bonito garnish — wheat and fish.

items.en: Chilled tomato
items.note: Plain chilled tomato is the most likely thing on this card to be both plant-based and grain-free — but izakaya versions arrive with an onion dressing or mayonnaise. Ask for it undressed.

items.ja: たたききゅうり(梅しそ和え)
items.en: Smashed cucumber dressed with pickled plum and shiso
items.note: Cucumber, umeboshi and shiso are plant foods, but the dressing usually includes soy sauce, mentsuyu or sesame oil with dashi. Ask what the 和え is made with.

items.en: Lightly pickled Chinese cabbage
items.note: Asazuke is cabbage, salt and kombu in the simplest form, but commercial pickling liquors routinely include soy sauce, amino-acid seasoning or bonito. Ask.

items.en: Nozawana greens pickled with wasabi
items.note: わさび漬け is traditionally made with 酒粕 (sake lees) and is commercially seasoned with soy sauce; the greens are also usually soy-marinated. Treat as wheat.

items.en: Raw octopus in wasabi
items.note: Octopus, and the wasabi paste is built on sake lees and soy seasoning.

items.en: Chanja — Korean-style spiced salted cod tripe
items.note: Fermented fish offal seasoned with gochujang, which is normally made with wheat flour as well as chilli, plus fish sauce.

items.en: Ume-suisho — shark cartilage with pickled plum
items.note: Shark cartilage; the standard seasoning is soy sauce and mirin, i.e. wheat.

items.en: Grilled dried skate fin
items.note: Dried fish, grilled over the yakitori fire and served with mayonnaise and shichimi — fish, egg, and a tare-splashed grill.

items.en: Seared vinegar-cured mackerel
items.note: Mackerel, and it is eaten with soy sauce; the cure itself often uses a kombu-and-vinegar base with mirin.

items.en: Plain white rice
items.note: Plain steamed Japanese rice is naturally grain-safe and plant-based — order it unseasoned, do not let anyone pour tare on it, and watch that the scoop has not been in something else. That is the survival option on this whole menu.

items.en: The closing bowl of ramen
items.note: ラーメンの麺＝小麦, and the soup is a soy or chicken tare. Wheat twice over.

items.ja: お茶漬け（梅・明太子・ねぎ納豆・野沢菜わさび）
items.en: Ochazuke — rice in tea/broth, choice of plum, mentaiko, spring-onion natto or wasabi nozawana
items.note: Ochazuke broth is made from a dashi packet or 白だし, which is soy sauce and therefore wheat as well as bonito. Every one of the four toppings is separately soy-seasoned.

items.ja: 信長謹製つくね月見丼
items.en: Tsukune rice bowl with a raw egg yolk
items.note: Tsukune is normally bound with panko or flour and glazed with soy tare; the yolk is raw egg.

items.en: 'Stupid-size' prawn crackers, party portion for 4–5 (mini portion for 2–3 at ¥418)
items.section: 信長名物 バカ盛り Party-size platters
items.note: Prawn crackers, i.e. shellfish; Japanese ebisen dough normally includes wheat flour alongside the starch, and they are fried in the shared oil.

items.ja: バカ盛りポテトフライ
items.en: 'Stupid-size' chips for 4–5 (mini for 2–3 at ¥528; three seasoning powders +¥100)
items.section: 信長名物 バカ盛り Party-size platters
items.note: Potato and oil are plant food, but they share a fryer with panko cutlets, spring rolls and takoyaki — a coeliac cannot eat from that oil. The flavour powders are also unspecified.

items.en: 'Stupid-size' green salad for 4–5 (mini for 2–3 at ¥638)
items.section: 信長名物 バカ盛り Party-size platters
items.note: The leaves are plant food; the dressing is not named. Japanese house dressings are usually soy or sesame based (wheat) and often contain egg. Ask for oil and salt.

items.en: 'Stupid-size' stir-fried bean sprouts for 4–5 (mini for 2–3 at ¥638)
items.section: 信長名物 バカ盛り Party-size platters
items.note: Bean sprouts are plant food, but a Japanese moyashi-itame is seasoned with soy sauce and/or an oyster or chicken-stock powder — wheat by default, and often not vegetarian either.

items.ja: 黒蜜ときな粉のバニラアイス
items.romaji: kuromitsu to kinako no vanilla ice
items.en: Vanilla ice cream with black sugar syrup and roasted soy flour
items.note: Dairy ice cream, so not vegan. Kuromitsu is cane sugar and kinako is roasted soybean — neither is a gluten grain, but commercial ice cream can carry a wheat-derived stabiliser. Ask.

tokyo_asakusa_tofa_king_asakus.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. THE SHOP'S OWN SITE IS GONE: to-fa.com no longer resolves at all (DNS failure on http and https, www and bare). The item list below therefore comes from two places and they are not equally fresh, so read the split carefully. (1) The douhua core — the three-step ordering card (①豆花を選びます / ②シロップを選びます / ③トッピングを選びます) — is transcribed from photographs of the shop's OWN laminated menu book taken 2026/06 and 2026/07, i.e. this summer. Those prices are current and are corroborated by dated 2026 diners: a 2026/06 review pays 豆花(小) ¥450 plus トッピング3種セット ¥350, exactly as printed. (2) The 軽食 (savoury), かき氷 and drink lists exist only on the shop's 公式 (shop-registered) Tabelog menu, 更新日 2017/12/14 for food and 2017/06/06 for drinks. That registration is demonstrably stale: it prices 豆花 150g at ¥400 and 300g at ¥500 where the 2026 card reads ¥450 and ¥550, and it omits the 四季春茶 a 2026/06 diner drank. So NO PRICE IS RECORDED for anything sourced only from the 2017 registration — the historical figure is quoted inside each note as context, not as a current price. Address 東京都台東区浅草4-43-4, roughly 15 minutes' walk north of Asakusa Station in a residential pocket; opened 2016-04-20; closed Tuesdays. The ordering system is the point: pick a base, pick a syrup (a, b and c are free and refills mid-bowl are free too), pile on as many toppings as you like. THERE IS NO ALLERGEN CHART AND NO GLUTEN-FREE CLAIM ANYWHERE. Almost everything in the sweet half of this shop is naturally wheat-free — soy, rice, tapioca, beans, jelly — but the same small kitchen also fries 油條 and griddles 葱抓餅, both pure wheat, so every 'naturally clear' item below is 'ask', not 'gf'. Tabelog files the shop under ベジタリアンメニューあり.

items.en: Douhua, small (150g) — the house dish. Silky warm-set soybean curd, softer and looser than tofu, eaten as a dessert with syrup and toppings. Available cold or hot. The shop's own English on the card: 'Soybean Curd (small 150g)'
items.section: ① 豆花を選びます Choose your douhua
items.note: Douhua is soy milk set with a coagulant — soy, water and a setting agent, with no wheat in the concept and no dairy or egg either, which is why this is one of the better dessert options in Tokyo for either diet. But the shop publishes no ingredient list and makes no claim, and it fries 油條 and griddles 葱抓餅 (both wheat) in the same small kitchen, so treat both flags as 'confirm'. The two questions to ask are what the coagulant is and whether the scoop is shared with the wheat side of the counter.

items.en: Douhua, large (300g). Cold or hot. The card's own warning: ※300gは豆腐一丁くらいになります — 300g is about a whole block of tofu, and 2026 diners repeatedly say even the small is bigger than expected
items.section: ① 豆花を選びます Choose your douhua
items.note: Same soy-and-coagulant base as the small. No wheat in the concept; no allergen statement from the shop; wheat is fried elsewhere in the kitchen. Confirm before relying on it.

items.en: Soy-milk douhua, small — the card explains it: 豆漿豆花とはシロップの代わりに豆乳をかけたものです, i.e. soy milk is poured over instead of syrup. Cold only
items.section: ① 豆花を選びます Choose your douhua
items.note: Soy on soy — the syrup is replaced by soy milk, so there is no sugar syrup of unknown composition involved, which makes this the cleanest-looking bowl on the card. Marked ★ on the menu, meaning the topping-liquid is fixed and you do not choose a syrup. Still 'ask' on both counts: no allergen statement, shared wheat kitchen, and commercial soy milk in Japan occasionally carries additives the shop has not declared.

items.en: Soy-milk douhua, large (300g). Cold only
items.section: ① 豆花を選びます Choose your douhua
items.note: As the small: soy milk instead of syrup, fixed (★) so no syrup choice. No allergen information published; shared kitchen with wheat.

items.ja: 愛玉子（オーギョーチィ）
items.en: Aiyu jelly — a pale, barely-sweet Taiwanese jelly set from the washed seeds of a climbing fig, with a texture nothing else has. The card serves it with Taiwanese calamansi syrup only, cold only. A handwritten sticker on the 2026 book adds 種から作る愛玉子 ¥600 要予約 — a from-the-seed version made to order on advance reservation
items.section: ① 豆花を選びます Choose your douhua
items.note: Aiyu is fig-seed pectin set in water — no grain, no gelatin, no dairy in the traditional preparation, so on paper this is the most diet-friendly thing in the building for either diet. The shop states only 愛玉子は台湾産シークワーサーシロップのみ (Taiwanese calamansi syrup only) and publishes nothing about ingredients, and the kitchen handles wheat, so both flags stay 'ask'. If you want the real thing, the ¥600 from-seed version needs booking ahead.

items.en: Grass jelly (xiancao) — near-black, faintly bitter-herbal jelly, the Taiwanese summer standard. Cold only, and the card fixes the syrup: 仙草ゼリーはきび砂糖シロップのみ（冷たいののみ）
items.section: ① 豆花を選びます Choose your douhua
items.note: Grass jelly is a decoction of the Mesona herb set with starch. Which starch matters and the shop does not say: potato, tapioca and sweet-potato starch are the usual ones and carry no gluten, but the shop makes no statement at all, and the kitchen handles wheat. Also sold as a 150-yen topping.

items.en: Hot grass jelly — the same herb served as a warm, loose, drinkable dessert rather than a set jelly. Hot only
items.section: ① 豆花を選びます Choose your douhua
items.note: Warm 燒仙草 is thickened rather than set, and the thickener is not declared. Usually a root starch (no gluten) but the shop publishes nothing and wheat is handled on the premises. Ask.

items.en: Peanut soup — whole peanuts simmered until they collapse, served warm and sweet. Hot only. The most expensive single bowl on the base list
items.section: ① 豆花を選びます Choose your douhua
items.note: Peanuts, water and sugar in the classic version — no grain, no dairy. Not declared by the shop, and obviously a serious allergen in its own right for anyone with a peanut allergy. The same peanut liquor is offered free as syrup (c) on the syrup card, which tells you the shop makes it in quantity.

items.en: Wooden-tub douhua, 1.3kg — the sharing format, 取り分けて大勢で食べるなら (if you're eating with a crowd). Comes with five toppings of your choice. The shop warns it is made to order and takes a good ten minutes, longer when busy
items.section: ① 豆花を選びます Choose your douhua
items.note: Same douhua, served fresh-made in a wooden tub with five toppings included — so the flags depend on which five you pick as much as on the base. No allergen statement; shared kitchen with wheat.

items.en: Cane sugar syrup — the default, and the one to have if you want to taste the soy. Free, and the card notes abcのシロップは無料 途中の追加もOKです — the free syrups can be topped up mid-bowl
items.section: ② シロップを選びます Choose your syrup
items.note: Unrefined cane sugar dissolved in water is the standard recipe and contains no grain and no animal product, but the shop declares nothing. 'Ask' rather than a claim.

items.ja: きび砂糖しょうがシロップ
items.en: Cane sugar and ginger syrup — the warming one, and the traditional pairing for hot douhua in winter. Free
items.section: ② シロップを選びます Choose your syrup
items.note: Cane sugar plus ginger. No declared ingredients. A 2026/06 diner ordered exactly this on a 豆花(小) at no extra charge, confirming the free pricing.

items.ja: ピーナッツスープシロップ
items.en: Peanut soup syrup — the shop's own 花生湯 used as the liquid. Free, cold only
items.section: ② シロップを選びます Choose your syrup
items.note: Peanut based, so a hard no for a peanut allergy even though it is free and looks innocuous on the card. The Tabelog registration flags it 数量限定 (limited quantity). No grain in the classic recipe; nothing declared.

items.ja: 黒ごまシロップ（芝麻糊）
items.en: Black sesame syrup — properly 芝麻糊, the thick roasted-sesame paste-pudding, poured over the douhua instead of a thin syrup. The most substantial upgrade on the card, and 2026 reviewers single it out
items.section: ② シロップを選びます Choose your syrup
items.note: 芝麻糊 is roasted black sesame ground with sugar and thickened — and the thickener is the question. Glutinous rice flour (no gluten despite the name) is the traditional one, but commercial versions sometimes use wheat starch, and Chinese-style sesame pastes are sometimes finished with milk. The shop declares nothing, so ask on both counts.

items.en: Almond (apricot-kernel) syrup — the annin-dofu flavour, as a pour
items.section: ② シロップを選びます Choose your syrup
items.note: Commercial 杏仁 syrups are frequently milk- or cream-based, which would defeat vegan; the shop declares nothing either way. No grain expected, but nothing is stated. Ask.

items.en: Vanilla syrup — the cheapest upgrade, and the one aimed at children
items.section: ② シロップを選びます Choose your syrup
items.note: A bought-in flavour syrup of undeclared composition. No reason to expect grain, but there is no label to read.

items.en: Boiled peanuts — the shop's own first recommendation, ★オススメ, described on the card as やわらかくてオススメ (soft, and we recommend it). The classic douhua topping in Taiwan
items.section: ③ トッピング（150円）Toppings, ¥150 each
items.note: Peanuts simmered soft in sugar water — legume, no grain, no animal product in the standard version. Nothing declared by the shop. Obviously off-limits with a peanut allergy, and note that this shop's free peanut syrup means peanut is everywhere in the room.

items.ja: 地瓜圓（さつまいも団子）
items.en: Sweet potato dumplings — small chewy orange balls. The card marks them ★オススメ and says お店で手作り (made in-house), which is unusual; most shops buy them in
items.section: ③ トッピング（150円）Toppings, ¥150 each
items.note: Sweet potato kneaded with starch — 地瓜粉 (sweet potato starch) or tapioca starch in the Taiwanese original, neither of which is a gluten grain. The shop says only that it makes them itself and lists no ingredients, and its kitchen also handles wheat flour for 葱抓餅 and 油條, which is exactly the scenario where a house-made dough matters. Ask what the flour is.

items.en: Tapioca pearls — the small old-fashioned kind rather than bubble-tea boba
items.section: ③ トッピング（150円）Toppings, ¥150 each
items.note: Tapioca is cassava starch — a root, not a grain, and naturally free of gluten. Nothing is declared here and pearls are boiled in shared water in a wheat-handling kitchen, so 'ask'. Also offered as a drink add-in.

items.en: Glutinous rice dumplings — soft white (and pink) rice balls. The card notes 紅白で可愛い, red-and-white and pretty
items.section: ③ トッピング（150円）Toppings, ¥150 each
items.note: A word worth decoding: 'glutinous' rice is a texture description and has nothing to do with gluten — mochigome is rice, and rice has no gluten. So a plain tangyuan is naturally clear. The shop declares nothing and the kitchen handles wheat, so confirm rather than assume, and check whether the pink colouring is anything more than colour.

items.ja: 仙草ゼリー（トッピング）
items.en: Grass jelly as a topping — cubed into the bowl. Marked ★オススメ
items.section: ③ トッピング（150円）Toppings, ¥150 each
items.note: Same jelly as the ¥500 base bowl: Mesona herb set with an undeclared starch. Root starches are usual and carry no gluten, but nothing is stated. One of the shop's own three recommended combinations pairs it with peanuts and tapioca as 台湾で人気の3種.

items.en: Taro dumplings — the purple-grey sibling of the sweet potato balls
items.section: ③ トッピング（150円）Toppings, ¥150 each
items.note: Taro kneaded with starch, same construction as the sweet potato dumpling and the same open question about which flour binds it. Ask.

items.ja: 2色団子（さつまいも団子・さといも団子）
items.en: Two-colour dumplings — the sweet potato and taro balls together, orange and purple in one scoop. Appears in the shop's own 'if you can't decide, have this' combination
items.section: ③ トッピング（150円）Toppings, ¥150 each
items.note: Both dumplings at once, so both open questions at once: the binding starch is not declared and the shop makes them itself in a kitchen that also handles wheat flour.

items.en: Black glutinous rice — simmered purple-black rice with a popping texture. The card's line: ビタミンとミネラルが豊富。ぷちぷちした食感 (rich in vitamins and minerals, a little pop to it). The shop lists it as a recommendation in its own right
items.section: ③ トッピング（150円）Toppings, ¥150 each
items.note: Another word trap in your favour: 'glutinous' rice contains no gluten. Black glutinous rice is rice, full stop — this is not a multigrain blend and there is no 押麦 or もち麦 hiding in it, which is the usual danger with anything Japanese described as a grain topping. Still 'ask' because the shop declares nothing and the kitchen handles wheat.

items.en: Sweetened red beans (azuki)
items.section: ③ トッピング（100円）Toppings, ¥100 each
items.note: Azuki simmered with sugar — a legume, no grain, no animal product in the standard preparation. Nothing declared by the shop.

items.en: Mung beans, simmered soft. The card's pitch: 女性に人気！解熱の作用アリ！ (popular with women; said to cool a fever)
items.section: ③ トッピング（100円）Toppings, ¥100 each
items.note: Mung bean is a legume, not a grain. No wheat expected; nothing declared. Appears in the shop's own 美肌 combination with Job's tears and white fungus.

items.en: White fungus (snow fungus, Tremella) — translucent, frilly, gently crunchy. The card says 女性に人気！コリコリ肌にいい (popular with women; a good crunch, good for the skin). Note the shop's own English label reads 'Wood Ear Mushroom', which is a mistranslation — 銀耳 is snow fungus, not the black kikurage
items.section: ③ トッピング（100円）Toppings, ¥100 each
items.note: A fungus simmered in sugar water — no grain and no animal product in the standard preparation. Nothing declared by the shop. Flagged here mainly because the English on the shop's own card will mislead you about what you are ordering.

items.en: Job's tears — plump pearly grains, simmered. The card's own English is 'Job's Tears' and its pitch is 女性に人気！肌にいい！
items.section: ③ トッピング（100円）Toppings, ¥100 each
items.note: READ THIS ONE CAREFULLY, because the Japanese name contains 麦 and the whole point of that character is usually 'barley, therefore gluten'. Here it does not mean barley: 薏仁 / はとむぎ is Coix lacryma-jobi, Job's tears, a different genus entirely, and it is not one of the gluten grains. What keeps it at 'ask' rather than better is supply, not botany — Japanese はとむぎ is routinely milled, blended and packed alongside 押麦 and barley tea, はとむぎ blends often contain actual barley, and barley is NOT on Japan's statutory allergen list so nobody is obliged to tell you. This shop declares nothing at all. If you are coeliac, this is the single item on the topping card worth a specific question.

items.en: Chia seeds. The card's line: 食物繊維が豊富なスーパーフード
items.section: ③ トッピング（100円）Toppings, ¥100 each
items.note: Chia is a seed, not a grain, and carries no gluten. Nothing declared by the shop; shared kitchen. A 2026/06 diner had it on a large douhua with tapioca, grass jelly and two-colour dumplings.

items.en: Three-topping set — the value option, printed on the card as お得です！: any three of the ¥150 toppings for ¥350, or ¥300 if all three come from the ¥100 row
items.note: A price bundle, not a dish — the flags depend entirely on which three you choose. Confirmed at ¥350 by a 2026/06 diner. The shop prints three suggested trios: 緑豆・はとむぎ・白きくらげ (its 'good for the skin' set), ピーナッツ・タピオカ・仙草ゼリー (台湾で人気の3種) and ピーナッツ・2色団子・仙草ゼリー (お店のおすすめ、迷ったらこれ).

items.ja: 芒果冰（台湾産マンゴーかき氷）
items.en: Mango shaved ice, made with Taiwanese mango — sold in three grades, 並 / 上 / 特上
items.note: On the shop's own 公式 Tabelog registration but not on the 2026 menu-book photographs, and the registration dates from 2017/12 where it read ¥750 / ¥1,300 / ¥2,400 — a registration that is 10% below the shop's current card on the items where both exist, so no current price is recorded here. Taiwanese mango ice is usually finished with condensed milk, which would defeat vegan; the shop states nothing. Confirm it is still sold before planning around it.

items.ja: 総合剉冰（豆類と団子の盛り合わせかき氷）
items.en: Assorted shaved ice with beans and dumplings — the toppings piled onto ice instead of douhua
items.note: From the 2017 shop registration (¥1,100 there), not from the 2026 card, so no current price is recorded. Built from the same beans and dumplings as the topping list, so the same open questions apply — chiefly what binds the house-made dumplings.

items.ja: 総合剉冰（豆類の盛り合わせかき氷）
items.en: Assorted shaved ice, beans only — the cheaper of the two assortments
items.note: From the 2017 registration (¥750 there); no current price recorded. Beans and ice only, so it dodges the dumpling-flour question that the fuller version raises.

items.ja: 愛玉子剉冰（愛玉子かき氷）
items.en: Aiyu jelly shaved ice
items.note: From the 2017 registration (¥750 there); no current price recorded. Fig-seed jelly over ice — no grain and no dairy in the classic version, nothing declared here.

items.en: Grass jelly shaved ice
items.note: From the 2017 registration (¥950 there); no current price recorded. Same undeclared setting starch as the grass jelly itself.

items.en: Taiwanese scallion pancake — the flaky griddled street-food flatbread, shredded and torn as it cooks. Still sold: a 2026/05 diner writes 葱の餅はまじで美味しいからおすすめ！！朝ごはんにぴったり (seriously good, perfect for breakfast)
items.note: WHEAT. A cong zhua bing is a laminated wheat-flour dough — the flour IS the dish, there is no version of it without. This is also the reason nothing else in the shop can be called gluten-free: this dough is rolled and griddled in the same small kitchen as everything above. Vegan is a genuine 'ask': the dough is usually just flour, water, oil and scallion, but many shops griddle it with an egg on top or fold one in, and the shop publishes no recipe. Priced ¥350 on the 2017 registration; no current price recorded.

items.ja: 花巻（中華蒸しパン、饅頭）
items.en: Steamed flower roll — a soft, faintly sweet steamed wheat bun
items.note: WHEAT. A steamed mantou-family bun is wheat flour and yeast. Vegan 'ask' only because some recipes enrich the dough with milk or lard while the plain Taiwanese version does not, and the shop says nothing. ¥250 on the 2017 registration; no current price recorded.

items.en: Youtiao — the long Chinese fried dough stick, eaten torn into soy milk
items.note: WHEAT, and deep-fried, so it also puts wheat into the shop's frying oil. Note this if you were hoping anything else here came out of a fryer. Vegan 'ask' — the dough is normally flour, water and leavening with no animal product, but nothing is declared. ¥200 on the 2017 registration; no current price recorded.

items.en: Savoury soy milk — the Taiwanese breakfast bowl, where hot soy milk is curdled at the table by the vinegar underneath it and eaten with torn youtiao
items.note: Marked 'no' rather than 'ask' for a specific reason: the dish is defined by the 油條 croutons torn into it, and this shop sells 油條, which is wheat. The standard seasoning is also vinegar plus soy sauce, and Japanese soy sauce is wheat-brewed by default. Vegan is 'ask' because the classic recipe includes 蝦米 (dried shrimp) and the shop publishes no recipe — worth asking, since without the shrimp and the youtiao it would otherwise be a plant-based bowl. ¥600 on the 2017 registration; no current price recorded.

items.ja: 塩麹豆花（豆花の塩麹漬け）
items.en: Douhua cured in shio-koji — the shop's own oddity, the sweet dish turned savoury with salted rice malt
items.note: 塩麹 is normally 米麹 — rice koji and salt, no gluten grain — but 麦麹 (barley koji) versions exist and are sold in the same Japanese supermarkets, and barley is not on Japan's statutory allergen list so a label need not say. The shop declares nothing. Ask which koji. ¥300 on the 2017 registration; no current price recorded.

items.ja: 口水鶏（よだれどり）単品
items.en: 'Mouth-watering chicken' — cold poached chicken under a numbing chilli-and-sesame dressing. Sold on its own or over rice
items.note: Chicken, so not vegan. The dressing is the gluten problem: a koushui ji sauce is built on soy sauce and Chinkiang vinegar, and Japanese soy sauce contains wheat by default with no tamari named here. ¥450 on the 2017 registration; no current price recorded.

items.en: Chicken rice — shredded poached chicken over rice, the Taiwanese lunch-counter staple
items.note: Chicken, so not vegan. The rice is dressed with a soy-based sauce and rendered chicken fat, and no gluten-free tamari is named — assume wheat. ¥500 on the 2017 registration, with 丼の大盛り listed at ¥800; no current price recorded.

items.en: Mouth-watering chicken over rice — the chilli-dressed chicken as a rice bowl
items.note: Chicken and a soy-sauce-based chilli dressing. Not vegan; assume wheat. ¥500 on the 2017 registration (¥800 for the large bowl); no current price recorded.

items.en: Black sesame tangyuan — glutinous rice balls with a molten black sesame centre, added to a bowl
items.note: Glutinous rice flour outside, ground black sesame and sugar inside — 'glutinous' is texture, not gluten, and rice flour carries none. The classic filling binds the sesame with lard, which would defeat vegan, and modern versions use vegetable shortening instead; the shop states neither. ¥200 on the 2017 registration and not on the 2026 topping card, so confirm it is still made.

items.ja: タピオカソイミルクティー（豆乳入り）
items.en: Bubble soy milk tea — made with soy milk rather than dairy, which is the shop's default across its milk drinks
items.note: Soy milk, not cow's milk, which is unusual and useful — the shop's whole drink list is built on 豆漿. Tea and tapioca carry no gluten; nothing is declared. From the shop's 2017 drink registration (¥400 there) and no current price is recorded, because that registration is provably out of date — it omits the 四季春茶 a 2026/06 diner was served.

items.en: Bubble soy milk coffee
items.note: Soy-based, so no dairy in the concept. ¥400 on the 2017 registration; no current price recorded.

items.ja: 仙草ソイミルクティー（豆乳入り）
items.en: Grass jelly soy milk tea — a 2026/05 diner ordered the douhua-and-drink set with exactly this
items.note: Still on sale in 2026 (a dated review names it), which is more than can be said for the whole 2017 list. Grass jelly's setting starch is undeclared, as elsewhere. ¥450 on the 2017 registration; no current price recorded.

items.en: Sweet soy milk, lightly sugared — the plain Taiwanese breakfast drink. Hot or iced

items.en: Black tea, hot or iced. A 2026/06 diner was served 四季春茶 (a Taiwanese four-seasons oolong) which does not appear on the 2017 list, so the tea line-up has moved on — ask what is actually poured
items.note: Tea leaves and water carry no gluten and no animal product; the shop makes no statement, and its milk drinks are soy-based rather than dairy. ¥400 on the 2017 registration; no current price recorded.

items.note: A canned/bottled Taiwanese soft drink; the shop declares nothing and the can is the label to read. ¥350 on the 2017 registration; no current price recorded.
