tokyo_ramen_nagi_butao_shibuya.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Every price below is read off the shop's OWN ticket machine (食券機), photographed at full resolution in 2026/04 and again in 2026/05 with identical figures, and the in-store customisation card was re-photographed in 2026/08 unchanged — so these are current, not a stale card. A 2026/06 diner's write-up quotes ラーメン ¥850 and 替玉 ¥100, matching the machine exactly. WATCH THE SHOP IDENTITY: the record's website field is https://n-nagi.com/shop/新宿ゴールデン街-本館-3-2/, whose slug says 'Shinjuku Golden Gai honkan' — but the page it serves is genuinely 「ラーメン凪 BUTAO 渋谷店」, 東京都渋谷区東1-3-1 カミニート1F, 8 minutes from Shibuya East exit, tel 03-3499-0390. The slug is just a WordPress artefact from a duplicated post; the address and phone confirm it is the right branch. Founded 2006-06-15, refitted 2020-03-02, 28 seats (6 counter + 4 tables x 6 per the door sign, which counts 24). Mon-Sat 10:00-22:30, Sun 10:00-20:00. Cash only at the ticket machine. Nagi Spirits' own menu page names the four BUTAO variants and describes the broth but publishes NO prices at all, which is why the machine photo is load-bearing. THERE IS NO ALLERGEN CHART, no allergen notice in the window, and no gluten-free option: this is a Hakata-style tonkotsu shop and the entire menu is built on a wheat noodle. What the shop does publish, in unusual detail, is a customisation card — five axes, all free — and that card is the most useful thing here for a traveller who cannot read the counter.

items.en: Ramen — the standard bowl, ticket-machine button ①, and the shop's own English name for it is 'Original King'. Nagi's own description: a thick pork-bone broth the founder Ikuta worked and reworked, balanced between creamy and frankly porky. Marked スタンダード on the customisation card
items.note: Wheat, unavoidably and twice over: the noodle is wheat (this is a Hakata-style thin straight noodle shop, and 替麺 comes in five firmness grades because that is what a wheat noodle does), and a tonkotsu tare is soy-sauce based, which in Japan means wheat by default with no tamari named anywhere. Pork bone broth and pork chashu, so nothing here is vegan either. There is no allergen chart in this shop and no gluten-free noodle.

items.en: Upgrade to Red King — the same bowl with the shop's chilli oil (辣油) worked into it. Ticket-machine button ②, bought as an add-on ticket alongside the ¥850 base
items.note: A variant of a wheat-noodle bowl, so still wheat. The card states the addition is 辣油 (chilli oil); the shop publishes nothing about what is in that oil, and Chinese-style chilli oils are frequently built on a soy or bean-paste base. Pork broth, so not vegan.

items.en: Upgrade to Black King — black and glossy, and the customisation card spells out why: 麻油 & イカスミ, burnt sesame oil plus squid ink. Ticket-machine button ③
items.note: Read the card before ordering this one: the black is squid ink, not just burnt garlic oil as at most shops. That is a mollusc, so it matters to a shellfish allergy and it is not something the English name 'Black King' tells you. Still a wheat noodle in a soy-based tare. Not vegan.

items.en: Upgrade to Green King — the odd one out, and the card explains it: バジル & チーズ, basil and cheese, stirred into a tonkotsu. A Nagi invention brought back from its overseas branches. Ticket-machine button ④
items.note: Wheat noodle, soy-based tare — and this variant adds dairy on top, so it is out for anyone avoiding milk as well. Not vegan on two counts (pork broth and cheese).

items.en: Special Ramen — the loaded bowl, ticket-machine button ⑤, with the full set of toppings. The shop's English on the door card is 'Special Ramen'
items.note: Wheat noodle plus every soy-marinated topping the shop makes — the seasoned egg and the chashu are both cured in soy sauce. The deluxe bowl is the most wheat-exposed, not the least. Not vegan.

items.en: Chashu ramen — the bowl buried in braised pork belly. Ticket-machine button ⑥, and the most expensive item on the machine
items.note: Wheat noodle; chashu is braised in a soy-sauce liquor. Note the customisation card lets you take chashu from 無し (none) up through 0.5枚, 1枚, 2枚, 3枚, 4枚, 5枚 to 〜10枚 free of charge on any bowl, so this button is about the volume, not access. Not vegan.

items.en: Ramen with a seasoned soft-boiled egg. Ticket-machine button ⑦, English 'Flavored Egg Ramen'
items.note: Wheat noodle, and the egg itself is a wheat item — an ajitama is marinated in soy sauce, which is why a boiled egg you would think of as safe is not. Not vegan.

items.en: Spring onion ramen — a heap of shredded green onion over the bowl. Ticket-machine button ⑧, English 'Green Onion Ramen', and the machine carries a handwritten strip marking it as the current recommendation
items.note: The vegetable on top does not change what is underneath: wheat noodle in a pork broth with a soy tare. Not vegan.

items.en: Extra noodles — the Hakata refill. The shop's own sign asks you to order it when you are about halfway through your noodles, ご注文は麺を半分ほど食べた頃合いで、スタッフにお声がけください, so the broth does not go cold. Choose the firmness again: バリカタ (very firm) / カタ (firm) / ふつう (normal) / やわ (soft) / 超やわ (very soft)
items.note: Wheat noodle, straight up. Included here mostly to decode the five firmness words, which is the one thing a counter here will actually ask you and the one place a traveller freezes.

items.en: A bowl of plain white rice. Ticket-machine has both sizes: regular and small
items.note: The only thing in this building that is not made of wheat. Plain Japanese rice, unseasoned — labelled simply 白めし / 'rice' on the machine, i.e. not takikomi and not fried, which are the two ways a rice bowl usually acquires soy sauce. Kept at 'ask' rather than better because this is a wheat kitchen with no allergen policy, the scoop is shared, and rice is served across a counter where noodles are being drained. Small size 白めし(小) is ¥150.

items.en: Small bowl of plain white rice
items.note: Same plain unseasoned rice as the regular size. Same caveat: no allergen handling, shared utensils, wheat everywhere else in the room.

items.en: Chashu rice bowl — braised pork over rice, the standard ramen-shop side
items.note: The chashu is braised in a soy-sauce liquor and the sauce goes onto the rice, so this is the rice bowl that is NOT the safe one. If you came here for the plain rice, buy 白めし, not this. Not vegan.

items.en: Seasoned soft-boiled egg, as a topping. ¥130 on both the ticket machine and the counter topping list
items.note: 味付 means marinated, and the marinade is soy sauce — wheat. A plain boiled egg would be fine; this one is not. Egg, so not vegan.

items.ja: チャーシュー（トッピング）
items.en: Extra braised pork, as a topping. ¥250 on the counter topping list. Note the customisation card offers chashu from 無し up to 〜10枚 as a free choice on any bowl, so this paid topping is for going further still
items.note: Soy-braised pork — wheat via the braising liquor. Not vegan.

items.en: Wood ear mushroom, shredded — the standard crunchy tonkotsu topping. ¥120 on the machine and on the counter list
items.note: The fungus itself carries no gluten and no animal product, which makes this look like the safe topping. It usually is not: ramen-shop kikurage is dressed before it goes on, commonly with sesame oil and soy sauce, and this shop declares nothing. Ask whether it is dressed. It also lands in a wheat bowl.

items.en: Extra spring onion. ¥120
items.note: Shredded raw green onion — no wheat ingredient of its own and no animal product. 'Ask' rather than better because the shop makes no allergen statement, prepares it in a wheat kitchen, and it goes into a wheat bowl.

items.en: Sheets of nori seaweed. ¥120
items.note: Plain toasted nori is seaweed and nothing else, but 味付海苔 (the seasoned kind) is glazed with soy sauce, and shops rarely say which they buy. Ask. Nori is also commonly farmed in waters where shrimp and crab mix, which some Japanese allergen charts declare.

items.en: The house chilli paste, named 一撃 ('one strike'). Free, and on the customisation card you set the level yourself: 無し (none), 0.5辛, 1辛, 2辛, 3辛, 4辛, 5辛, up to 〜10辛
items.note: The shop calls it 秘製 — its own secret recipe — and publishes nothing about what is in it. Japanese ramen chilli pastes are commonly built on miso or soy, either of which would carry wheat (and miso can be 麦味噌, i.e. barley, which Japanese labelling law does not require anyone to declare). If you are coeliac and eating here anyway, order it 無し. Free at every level, which is unusual and worth knowing.

items.en: Noodle firmness — free, and you will be asked. The card's five settings: バリカタ (barikata, very firm, barely cooked) / カタ (kata, firm) / 普通 (futsū, normal) / 柔 (yawa, soft) / 超柔 (chō-yawa, very soft). The shop circles 普通 as its recommendation; the 2026 photographed card has カタ circled by the diner
items.note: Not a dish — this is the axis the counter will ask you about, and getting the word out is the difference between eating what you wanted and nodding blankly. The noodle itself is wheat at every firmness.

items.ja: 味の濃さ / こってり度 / にんにく
items.en: Three more free dials on the same card. 味の濃さ (seasoning strength): 薄い weak / 普通 normal / 濃い strong. こってり度 (richness, i.e. how much back-fat): 無し none / あっさり light / 普通 normal / こってり rich / 超こってり extra rich. にんにく (garlic): 無し none / 少々 a little / 普通 normal / 多い lots / 超多い loads. The shop circles 普通 on all three as its house setting
items.note: Worth knowing that 味の濃さ is literally the amount of soy-based tare, so 薄い means less wheat seasoning — but 'less' is not 'none' and this is not a bowl a coeliac can order at any setting. Included as decoding: these three dials plus noodle firmness and chilli level are all free, which makes this one of the most adjustable bowls in Shibuya.

items.en: Beer or highball — one ticket-machine button covers both
items.note: Both options fail: beer is barley malt, and a Japanese highball is whisky, which is distilled from malted barley. Never gluten-free either way.

items.en: Cola. The only soft drink on the machine
items.note: Cola is carbonated water, sugar, caramel colour, phosphoric acid, caffeine and flavourings — no grain ingredient, and it comes sealed, so nothing in this kitchen touches it. The one item in the building a coeliac can order without a conversation.

tokyo_sharin_shinjuku_center_b.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Tax-included, from the shop-managed (公式) Tabelog menu, 更新日 2026/04/08. 舎鈴 is the everyday-price arm of 松富士食品 (the 六厘舎 group); the branch page is shop.mtfj.co.jp/stores/55, 新宿センタービル B1F. The chain publishes prices only on the branch/Tabelog listing, not on tsukemen-sharin.com, so bowl prices are chain-standard rather than branch-verified — but the branch page carries no price variation notice. The allergen data below is far better sourced than the prices: the chain's own PDF アレルゲン情報 chart, dated 2026年8月21日, gives a 28-allergen row for every single bowl, topping and side. USE THE 関東エリア PAGE (page 1) — page 2 is 関西エリア and the rows differ. The chart's own footnote is the important part for a coeliac: 「当店で使用している調理器具・食器は商品ごとに使い分けをしておりません」— utensils and bowls are NOT separated by product, and the chain says secondary contamination cannot be prevented.

items.en: Tsukemen — the house bowl. Custom medium-thick chewy noodles served cold beside a hot pork-and-chicken dipping broth, rich but with a clean finish. Small ¥790 / regular ¥890 / large ¥990 / extra-large ¥1,090, all the same price for more noodles
items.note: The chain's own 2026-08-21 allergen chart marks つけめん for えび・かに・小麦・卵・乳 plus 牛肉・ごま・さけ・さば・大豆・鶏肉・豚肉・りんご・ゼラチン. 小麦 is the noodle (the shop's own copy boasts 小麦の風味を生かした特注中太麺) and the soy-sauce tare. Gelatin and four kinds of meat and fish rule out vegan. Sharin's chart also warns the soup ingredients are landed by a fishery where shrimp and crab mix.

items.en: Tsukemen with a seasoned soft-boiled egg — served whole and uncut so the yolk stays in. Small ¥940 / regular ¥1,040 / large ¥1,140 / extra-large ¥1,240
items.note: Chart row: えび・かに・小麦・卵・乳 plus the same meats. The 味玉 has its own row and is itself marked 小麦 — the egg is marinated in soy sauce.

items.en: Dandan tsukemen — a sesame-and-chilli dipping broth done as tsukemen rather than as noodle soup. Small ¥940 / regular ¥1,040 / large ¥1,140 / extra-large ¥1,240
items.note: The only bowl on the chart that also carries 落花生 (peanut) alongside えび・かに・小麦・卵・乳. Wheat noodle and wheat tare.

items.en: Deluxe tsukemen — extra chashu, extra seasoned egg, extra nori. Small ¥1,090 / regular ¥1,190 / large ¥1,290 / extra-large ¥1,390
items.note: Chart: えび・かに・小麦・卵・乳. The 特製盛り topping row is separately marked 小麦・卵 — chashu, seasoned egg and nori are all soy-marinated, so the deluxe adds wheat rather than avoiding it.

items.en: 'Founding' tsukemen — the original recipe. The chain's own menu page notes 一部店舗は未販売, so it may not be sold at this branch
items.note: On the allergen chart (with 創業味玉つけめん and 創業チャーシューつけめん) as えび・かに・小麦・卵・乳. Not on the Tabelog price list for this branch and no price is published anywhere, so no price is recorded here rather than a guessed one.

items.en: Ramen — a faintly aromatic niboshi (dried-sardine) broth with the depth of dark soy, and firm hand-rubbed wrinkled noodles. Regular ¥790 / large ¥890
items.note: Chart: えび・かに・小麦・卵・乳 plus さけ・さば・大豆・鶏肉・豚肉. 濃口醤油 is the stated seasoning — wheat soy sauce — on top of the wheat noodle. The chart adds that the chain's noodles contain NO egg except the miso-ramen noodle, so the 卵 mark here is the topping, not the strand.

items.en: Ramen with a seasoned soft-boiled egg, served uncut. Regular ¥940 / large ¥1,040
items.note: Chart: えび・かに・小麦・卵・乳. Both the noodle and the egg's marinade are wheat.

items.en: Deluxe ramen — extra chashu, seasoned egg and nori. Regular ¥1,090 / large ¥1,190
items.note: Chart: えび・かに・小麦・卵・乳 plus the meats. Every element of the 特製 topping set is separately marked 小麦.

items.en: Plain ramen — noodles and broth with nothing on top. The chart's leanest bowl
items.note: The chart marks 素らーめん for only えび・かに・小麦 plus 大豆・鶏肉 — no egg, no dairy. Still wheat: the noodle and the tare. Included because it is on the chain's own allergen chart; no price is published for it, so none is recorded.

items.en: Morning ramen, served at branches that open early
items.note: Chart: えび・かに・小麦 plus 大豆・鶏肉・豚肉 — no egg or dairy unless you add 味玉. Wheat noodle. No published price.

items.en: Chilled kake ramen — cold broth over cold noodles, a summer bowl. Also sold with myoga, oni-oroshi daikon, shirasu-oroshi or coriander
items.note: Chart: えび・かに・小麦・卵・乳 for all five 冷やかけ variants. Cold does not make it wheat-free — same noodle, same soy tare. No published price.

items.en: Miso ramen (with 味玉 and 特製 versions)
items.note: Chart: えび・かに・小麦・卵・乳 plus 牛肉・ごま. The chain's footnote singles this one out — 「味噌ラーメン」の麺には「卵」が含まれております。その他の麺には「卵」を使用しておりません — so the miso bowl is the only one with an egg noodle. No published price.

items.en: Soup-wari — the thin broth poured into your leftover dipping tare at the end to drink it
items.note: Interesting and genuinely useful: the chart marks the スープ割 broth for only えび・かに・大豆 — NO 小麦 of its own. But it goes into a bowl of wheat-bearing dipping tare, so it does not make anything gluten-free; it just tells you the wheat lives in the tare and the noodle, not the stock.

items.en: Braised pork chashu, as a topping
items.note: Own chart row: 小麦 plus オレンジ・大豆・鶏肉・豚肉・ゼラチン. Braised in a soy-sauce liquor — wheat. No published price.

items.en: Seasoned soft-boiled egg, as a topping
items.note: Own chart row: 小麦・卵 plus さば・大豆. The wheat is the soy-sauce marinade — a plain boiled egg would not be marked. No published price.

items.en: Sheet nori, as a topping
items.note: Own chart row: 小麦・卵. Seaweed itself is neither, so this is a seasoned/glazed nori. The chart also states 海苔は、エビ、カニが混ざる地域で養殖しています — farmed where shrimp and crab mix. No published price.

items.en: Fermented bamboo shoot, as a topping
items.note: Own chart row: 小麦・乳 plus ごま・大豆・鶏肉. Bamboo shoot is a vegetable but this menma is seasoned with soy sauce, dairy and chicken stock. No published price.

items.en: Spinach, as a topping
items.note: The chart row for ほうれん草 is completely blank — none of the 28 allergens, including 小麦. That is the chain's own statement that this topping carries no wheat ingredient. It is still 'ask', not 'gf', because the chart's own footnote says utensils and bowls are not separated by product and secondary contamination cannot be prevented, and it lands in a wheat broth. No published price.

items.en: Extra spring onion
items.note: Blank row on the chain's allergen chart — no wheat ingredient declared. Same shared-utensil caveat as the spinach. No published price.

items.en: The deluxe topping set — extra chashu, seasoned egg and nori in one
items.note: Own chart row: 小麦・卵 plus オレンジ・さけ・さば・大豆・鶏肉・豚肉・ゼラチン. No published price.

items.en: A bowl of plain rice
items.note: The most useful line on the whole chart for a coeliac in a ramen shop: the ライス row is entirely blank — no 小麦, no anything, and the footnote says 当店のライスは、国産米を使用しております. So the rice itself is plain Japanese rice with nothing added. It stays 'ask' rather than 'gf' only because the chain states in the same document that cooking utensils and tableware are not separated by product, so a shared scoop in a wheat kitchen is a live risk. No published price.

items.en: Fried rice
items.note: Chart: 小麦・卵 plus オレンジ・大豆・鶏肉・豚肉・ゼラチン. Fried rice is seasoned with soy sauce — wheat — which is exactly why plain ライス is safe and this is not.

items.en: Chashu over rice
items.note: Chart: 小麦 plus オレンジ・さけ・大豆・鶏肉・豚肉・ゼラチン. The chashu's soy braise is the wheat. Same for ネギチャーシュー丼.

items.en: Seasoned-egg rice bowl
items.note: Chart: 小麦・卵 plus さけ・さば・大豆・豚肉. Soy-marinated egg over rice.

items.en: Dandan rice bowl
items.note: Chart: 小麦 plus さけ・大豆・豚肉.

items.en: Gyoza — the chain's menu page flags them as sold only at certain branches (→販売店舗)
items.note: Chart: 小麦・乳 plus 牛肉・ごま・大豆・鶏肉・豚肉・ゼラチン. 餃子の皮＝小麦 — the wrapper is wheat, as always. Check whether the Shinjuku Center Building branch sells them at all.

items.en: Myoga ginger bud — topping
items.note: Blank row on the chain's own 2026-08-21 allergen chart — none of the 28 allergens declared, so no wheat ingredient of its own. It still goes into a wheat bowl and the chart's footnote states 「当店で使用している調理器具・食器は商品ごとに使い分けをしておりません」— utensils and crockery are NOT separated by product, so secondary contamination cannot be excluded. No published price.

items.en: Coarsely grated daikon — topping
items.note: Blank row on the chain's own allergen chart — no declared allergen, i.e. plain grated daikon with no soy seasoning. Same shared-utensil caveat as the other blank rows. No published price.

items.en: Grated daikon with whitebait — topping
items.note: Whitebait — fish, so not vegan. The chart row is blank for all 28 allergens (しらす is not itself a listed allergen), so no wheat is declared, but shared utensils apply. No published price.

items.en: Coriander leaf — topping
items.note: Blank row on the chain's own allergen chart — a plain herb, no declared allergen. Shared utensils apply. No published price.

items.en: Lemon — topping
items.note: Blank row on the chain's own allergen chart. Shared utensils apply. No published price.

items.en: Children's ramen — sold as a single bowl or as a set
items.note: Chart: えび・かに・小麦・卵・乳 plus オレンジ・さけ・さば・大豆・鶏肉・豚肉・ゼラチン; the セット version adds もも・りんご and やまいも. Wheat noodle and wheat tare — a children's portion is not a milder allergen profile. No published price.

items.ja: 茗荷冷やかけ / 鬼おろし冷やかけ / しらすおろし冷やかけ / パクチー冷やかけ
items.en: Chilled 'hiyakake' ramen — myoga, grated daikon, whitebait or coriander versions
items.note: All four variants carry えび・かに・小麦・卵・乳 on the chain's own chart, exactly like the plain 冷やかけ. The blank-row garnish on top does not rescue the bowl underneath. No published prices.

items.en: Frozen raw gyoza, to take home
items.note: Chart: 小麦・乳 plus 牛肉・ごま・大豆・鶏肉・豚肉・ゼラチン. 餃子の皮＝小麦. No published price.

items.en: Loosening broth — added to every delivery/takeout tsukemen
items.note: Chart row: えび・かに plus 大豆 only — NO 小麦 declared, the same as スープ割. Shellfish, so not vegan (and the chart notes 「スープで使用している材料は、エビ、カニが混ざる漁法で捕獲しています」). The chart states this is attached to all delivery tsukemen. Interesting on its own, but it is poured into a wheat bowl.

tokyo_mugi_no_oto.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Tax-included. The shop's own site mugioto.com carries no menu at all, only hours and an Instagram link, so the item list comes from the shop-managed Gurunavi page r.gnavi.co.jp/geum9ft30000 (address on it: 東京都新宿区歌舞伎町1-12-15, matching mugioto.com's 新宿第7ビル B1). Confidence is medium for one reason: the Gurunavi prices and the Tabelog registration (更新日 2025/07/31) DISAGREE on two dishes — the Awaji beef rump is ¥2,800 on Gurunavi and ¥2,600 on Tabelog, the Nagano duck ¥1,800 vs ¥1,700. Gurunavi is taken as the newer figure and the Tabelog one is given in the note. Two dishes on the Tabelog list (the Nagasaki amberjack carpaccio ¥1,800 and the two 自家製 dolci at ¥800/¥900) are absent from Gurunavi and vice versa; both sets are recorded, flagged. Hours 18:00–05:00 Tue–Sun. The kitchen accepts allergy requests — the course pages state 「※アレルギーがございましたら当日スタッフまでお申し付けください」 — but publishes no allergen chart, so every gf/vegan value below is reasoning from the dish name. THE NAME IS A WARNING: 麦ノ音 means 'the sound of BARLEY'; this is a craft-beer bar with six rotating taps, and barley is a gluten grain.

items.ja: 群馬県川場産ブラッタチーズと季節果実のカプレーゼ
items.romaji: Gunma Kawaba-san burrata to kisetsu kajitsu no caprese
items.en: Caprese of Kawaba (Gunma) burrata with the season's fruit — figs from Wakayama at the time the Tabelog card was written
items.note: Burrata is dairy — not vegan. No wheat ingredient is implied by the dish, but the kitchen serves garlic toast and pasta and publishes no allergen information; ask whether anything crisp comes with it.

items.ja: 長崎県産カンパチの炙りカルパッチョ
items.en: Seared carpaccio of Nagasaki amberjack
items.note: Raw fish — not vegan. On the Tabelog registration (2025/07/31) but NOT on the current Gurunavi card, so it may have rotated off; check the board. Carpaccio dressing is not published and Japanese kitchens frequently mix soy sauce into it — wheat.

items.ja: スペイン産生ハムと今夜のチーズ達
items.romaji: Spain-san nama-hamu to kon'ya no chīzu-tachi
items.en: Spanish cured ham with tonight's cheeses
items.note: Cured pork and dairy — not vegan. Jamón and cheese are not wheat in themselves; the risk is the crackers, grissini or bread that come with a cheese plate. Ask for it without.

items.en: Snack platter, three items — a four-item version is ¥3,000
items.note: Composition is chosen on the night from the bar snacks, so nothing can be said in advance. The individual components sold separately are パルミジャーノ (dairy), 野菜マリネ (marinated vegetables — the plant option) and プロシュート (pork), each ¥500 on their own. Specify what you can eat when you order.

items.ja: パルミジャーノ / 野菜マリネ / プロシュート（各単品）
items.en: Single snack plates — Parmigiano, marinated vegetables, or prosciutto, ¥500 each
items.note: The 野菜マリネ is the one plausibly plant-only plate on the whole card — marinated vegetables, ¥500. The marinade is not published; ask about anchovy and honey. Parmigiano is dairy and, being an aged cheese, is made with animal rennet as standard; prosciutto is pork.

items.ja: 北あかりのハンドクラフトポテト　アンチョビとパルミジャーノ
items.romaji: Kitaakari no handcraft potato, anchovy to Parmigiano
items.en: Hand-cut Kitaakari-potato chips with anchovy and Parmigiano
items.note: Anchovy and Parmigiano — fish and dairy, so firmly not vegan. Hand-cut potatoes are usually unfloured, but this is a bar fryer that also handles the garlic fritto and possibly breaded items; ask.

items.ja: 自家製白レバーペーストとガーリックトースト
items.romaji: jikasei shiro-lever paste to garlic toast
items.en: House-made pale chicken-liver pâté with garlic toast — the Gurunavi version adds semi-dried tomato
items.note: Chicken liver — not vegan. The toast is wheat bread and it is part of the dish, not a side. Ask whether the pâté alone can be served with something else.

items.ja: 長野県産ニンニクのほくほくフリットとスペイン産生ハム
items.romaji: Nagano-san ninniku no hokuhoku fritto to Spain-san nama-hamu
items.en: Fluffy fritters of Nagano garlic with Spanish cured ham
items.note: Cured pork — not vegan. フリット is a battered fritter, and a fritto batter is wheat flour (often with beer in it, which in a craft-beer bar is a real possibility). Wheat.

items.ja: 淡路牛肉ランプのステーキ　夏野菜のロースト添え
items.romaji: Awaji gyūniku rump no steak, natsu-yasai no roast-zoe
items.en: Awaji beef rump steak with roasted summer vegetables
items.note: Beef — not vegan. PRICE CONFLICT: ¥2,800 on the shop's Gurunavi card, ¥2,600 on its Tabelog registration of 2025/07/31; the newer Gurunavi figure is used. Plain grilled beef carries no wheat, but the sauce is not published and a soy or balsamic-soy jus is common. Ask.

items.ja: ソーセージフェストのクラフトソーセージグリル
items.romaji: Sausage Fest no craft sausage grill
items.en: Grilled craft sausages from Sausage Fest — the additive-free organic maker selected for the Michelin Guide 2018 Bib Gourmand. The house signature and the fixed centrepiece of both courses
items.note: Pork sausage — not vegan. This is the dish to ask about: sausage is one of the classic hidden-wheat products (rusk, breadcrumb or wheat-starch binder is standard in Japan, and the casing may be collagen), but the shop describes this maker as 無添加オーガニック — additive-free organic — which sometimes means a meat-only formulation. The maker is named, so it is answerable at the counter. Do not assume either way.

items.ja: 長野県産鴨の低温ロースト　青梅野菜のマリネ添え
items.romaji: Nagano-san kamo no teion roast, Ōme yasai no marine-zoe
items.en: Low-temperature roast Nagano duck with marinated Ome-grown vegetables
items.note: Duck — not vegan. PRICE CONFLICT: ¥1,800 on Gurunavi, ¥1,700 on the 2025/07/31 Tabelog card; the newer figure is used. Sous-vide duck breast is usually just duck, salt and aromatics, but Japanese duck is very often brined in soy sauce — ask.

items.en: Tonight's pasta — changes daily; also the closing dish of both set courses
items.note: Pasta is wheat and no gluten-free alternative is offered. Since the sauce changes nightly a plant-based version may be possible on request — the shop does invite allergy requests on the day — but the noodle itself rules out coeliac diners.

items.ja: 自家製クラシックショコラ
items.en: House-made classic chocolate cake
items.note: On the Tabelog registration; the current Gurunavi card lists rum-soaked Baumkuchen and house catalana at ¥800 instead, so the dessert list rotates. Classic chocolat is flour, butter and egg — not vegan, treat as wheat.

items.ja: 自家製フィナンシェと季節のフルーツ
items.romaji: jikasei financier to kisetsu no fruit
items.en: House-made financier with seasonal fruit
items.note: On the Tabelog registration (2025/07/31), not on the current Gurunavi card. A financier is beurre-noisette, egg white, almond and WHEAT flour. Not vegan, not gluten-free.

items.ja: ラム酒に漬けたバームクーヘンと季節のフルーツ
items.romaji: rum-shu ni tsuketa Baumkuchen to kisetsu no fruit
items.en: Rum-soaked Baumkuchen with seasonal fruit
items.note: On the current Gurunavi card. Baumkuchen is a wheat-flour, egg and butter cake. Not vegan, not gluten-free.

items.ja: 自家製カタラーナと季節のフルーツ
items.romaji: jikasei catalana to kisetsu no fruit
items.en: House-made crema catalana with seasonal fruit
items.note: On the current Gurunavi card. Crema catalana is milk, egg yolk and sugar — not vegan. It is one of the few desserts with no flour in the recipe itself, which makes it the best dessert bet for a coeliac here; ask whether a biscuit is served alongside.

items.ja: 【2H飲放】スタンダードコース 6品
items.en: Standard course, 6 dishes, with 2 hours of free-flow drinks including one craft beer — today's starter, one or two cold plates, one or two hot plates, the Sausage Fest craft sausage grill, and the pasta of the day. 4–10 people, arrivals 18:00–23:00
items.note: Per person. The course ends on the pasta of the day — wheat — and centres on the pork sausage, so it works for neither diet as sold. The shop does say 「※アレルギーがございましたら当日スタッフまでお申し付けください」, so substitutions are worth raising when booking. The free-flow list includes 生ビール, ハイボール and 麦焼酎, all barley.

items.en: Premium course — the same 6 dishes with 3 hours of free-flow drinks off a longer list. 4–10 people, arrivals 17:00–03:00
items.note: Per person. Same food as the standard course — pasta and pork sausage — so the same answers. Allergy requests taken on the day.

items.en: Eight seasonal dishes for a special occasion; contents change with the season and the shop asks you to phone for details. 2–80 people, arrivals 17:00–03:00, 3 hours
items.note: Per person. The shop publishes no dish list at all — 「季節ごとに食材や料理内容が変わりますので詳細はお店にお問い合わせください」 — so nothing can be stated about it. Because it is built to order and the shop takes allergy requests, it is the one item here worth a phone call for either diet.

items.ja: クラフトビール（常時6タップ）
items.en: Craft beer — six taps kept live, shipped direct from talked-about breweries and rotated weekly; many cans and bottles as well
items.note: This is the reason the bar exists and it is barley malt in every case — a gluten grain, never gluten-free. Many craft beers also use WHEAT (witbier, hefeweizen) and oats. Vegan status varies by brewery: fining with isinglass or gelatine and additions of honey or lactose are all common in craft brewing.

items.en: Suntory The Premium Malt's draught
items.note: 'Malt's' is the name and the ingredient: 100% barley malt. Not gluten-free.

items.en: Natural wine — the other half of the concept; ask the staff and they will bring a bottle matched to your food
items.note: Natural wine is actually the best drink question to ask here: low-intervention winemaking often means NO fining at all, which is exactly what makes a wine vegan — and unlike the beer there is no grain in it. Ask the staff whether the bottle is unfined and unfiltered; they choose the list themselves.

items.ja: グラスワイン　白・赤
items.en: House wine by the glass, white or red
items.note: Grape, not grain. Fining agents (egg white, casein, gelatine, isinglass) are the vegan question and are not published for the house pour. Bottles from ¥3,000.

items.ja: JAPANESE WHISKEY（角／富士山麓／余市／白州／山崎／知多）
items.en: Japanese whisky — Kaku, Fujisanroku, Yoichi, Hakushu, Yamazaki, Chita
items.note: Malted BARLEY (Chita is a grain whisky, i.e. corn and barley malt). Distillation removes most gluten protein but this app does not flag malt spirits as gluten-free.

items.ja: WHISKEY（カナディアンクラブ／ジャックダニエル／メーカーズマーク／マッカラン／ラフロイグ）
items.en: Imported whisky — Canadian Club, Jack Daniel's, Maker's Mark, Macallan, Laphroaig
items.note: All grain spirits; Maker's Mark's mash bill includes WHEAT and Canadian Club includes rye. Not treated as gluten-free.

items.en: Shochu of the month
items.note: Which shochu decides the answer. 麦焼酎 is distilled from BARLEY; 芋 (sweet potato) and 米 (rice) are not gluten grains. The free-flow course lists carry both 芋 and 麦 explicitly, so both are in the building — name the base when you order.

items.en: Sake of the month
items.note: Sake is rice, water, koji and yeast — no gluten grain, and the koji on sake is rice koji not barley. The residual questions are whether any 醸造アルコール is grain-derived and whether the brewery fines with gelatine; neither is published here.

items.ja: サワー（レモン／グレープフルーツ／ジンジャーハイ／コークハイ／緑茶ハイ／ウーロンハイ／ジャスミンハイ／麦茶ハイ／梅酒）
items.en: Sours and highballs — lemon, grapefruit, ginger, cola, green tea, oolong, jasmine, BARLEY TEA, or umeshu
items.note: READ THE LIST: 麦茶ハイ is barley-tea shochu — 麦茶 is roasted BARLEY, a gluten grain, and it is on this menu as a mixer. The base spirit for the sours may also be 麦焼酎. Green tea, oolong and jasmine highballs avoid the barley in the mixer but not necessarily in the spirit; ask for an imo-shochu base.

items.ja: カクテル（カシスオレンジ／シャンディ・ガフ／モスコミュール／ジントニック／レゲェパンチ／マリブミルク／カルーアミルク ほか）
items.en: Cocktails — cassis orange, shandy gaff, moscow mule, gin & tonic, reggae punch, Malibu milk, Kahlúa milk and more
items.note: One name on this list is a beer cocktail: シャンディ・ガフ is beer and ginger ale, so it is BARLEY and not gluten-free. レッドアイ (on the course lists) is beer and tomato juice, same problem. マリブミルク and カルーアミルク contain dairy. Vodka and gin may be grain-distilled.

items.ja: ソフトドリンク（コーラ／ジンジャエール／レモンスカッシュ／マンゴー／クランベリー／ウーロン茶／緑茶）
items.en: Soft drinks — cola, ginger ale, lemon squash, mango, cranberry, oolong tea, green tea
items.note: No grain ingredient implied by any of these, and note that the soft-drink list — unlike the sour list — contains no 麦茶. Brands not published.

items.ja: Ne10 GIN（歌舞伎町クラフトジン）200ml
items.en: Ne10 — the Kabukicho original craft gin, sold as a 200 ml bottle to take away
items.note: A bottle to take home rather than a drink at the bar; the shop's own site links to ne10.ethicalspirits.jp. Gin's base spirit can be grain (usually wheat or barley) or molasses/rice — Ethical Spirits is known for redistilling spent material, so the base is worth asking about specifically. Not assessed here.

tokyo_tofu_ryori_sorano_shibuy.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Tax-included, from the Tabelog menu registration, 更新日 2025/04/09 — about sixteen months old at the time of checking, so treat the figures as indicative; the spring items (筍 bamboo shoot, タラの芽, 新じゃがいも, 新玉ねぎ, 桜鯛) are a SPRING card and will not all be on the board in August. The operator's own site, foodgate.net/shop/sorano (FOODGATE Co., Ltd., which also runs ごはんや一芯, 板蕎麦香り家, うどん山長 and others), carries the shop's philosophy, address and hours but no prices — hence `partial`, not `authoritative`. Address confirmed on both: 渋谷区桜丘町4-17 チェリーガーデン 1F, 5 min from the Shibuya south-exit west gate; 110 seats; Mon–Fri 17:00–22:45, Sat 16:30–22:45, Sun/hols 16:30–22:30. The one genuinely useful sourced fact for these diets is the operator's own line: 「『空野』では添加物や凝固剤を使用しない豆腐作りを一番に考えております」 — the tofu is made without additives or chemical coagulant, and the Tabelog card says the tofu is set AT YOUR TABLE from fresh soy milk with 天然にがり (natural nigari), from top-grade Hokkaido Tokachi トヨマサリ organic whole soybeans extracted at 14 degrees soy-milk density. No allergen chart is published; everything else below is reasoning from the dish name.

items.en: The house tofu, small — fresh soy milk brought to your table and set into tofu in front of you with natural nigari, eaten the moment it forms. Minimum two portions
items.note: This is the dish to come for and the one worth asking about carefully. The tofu itself is soybeans, water and 天然にがり (magnesium chloride) — no wheat, no animal ingredient, and the operator states it uses no additives or chemical coagulant. What decides both answers is WHAT COMES WITH IT: warm fresh tofu is served in Japan with soy sauce (wheat), a dashi-shoyu (wheat and bonito), or simply salt. Ask for salt and this becomes both gluten-free and vegan; take the default dip and it is neither.

items.en: Avocado tofu
items.note: Avocado and soy — both plant foods, and the cheapest thing on the card. The dressing is not published; a Japanese avocado-tofu is usually finished with soy sauce or a wasabi-soy, which would be wheat. Ask what it is dressed with.

items.en: Morning-made yuba (soy-milk skin), served raw like sashimi
items.note: Yuba is nothing but the skin lifted off simmering soy milk — plant, and no wheat. Again the dip decides it: yuba sashimi is served with soy sauce or a dashi-shoyu as standard. Ask for salt or ask what the tsuyu is made of. One of the two best candidates on this menu for either diet.

items.ja: 合鴨と生湯葉のおろしポン酢
items.romaji: aigamo to nama-yuba no oroshi ponzu
items.en: Duck and fresh yuba with grated daikon and ponzu
items.note: Duck — not vegan. Ponzu is citrus PLUS soy sauce plus bonito dashi, so it is wheat as well; and duck breast in a Japanese kitchen is usually brined in soy.

items.ja: 昆布〆桜鯛のカルパッチョ
items.en: Kelp-cured spring sea bream, carpaccio-style
items.note: Raw fish — not vegan. A SPRING item (桜鯛); may not be on the board out of season. 昆布〆 is a kelp cure, which is wheat-free in itself, but carpaccio dressings here are unpublished and Japanese kitchens routinely add soy.

items.ja: 中落ちサーモンとアボカドのユッケ
items.romaji: nakaochi salmon to avocado no yukke
items.en: Scraped salmon belly and avocado, dressed yukhoe-style with a raw egg yolk
items.note: Salmon and (as standard for yukke) raw egg yolk — not vegan. A yukke dressing is soy sauce, sesame oil, garlic and sugar; the soy is wheat.

items.ja: おからのポテトサラダ
items.en: Potato salad made with okara, the soy pulp left from making the tofu
items.note: Okara is a by-product of this shop's own tofu — a nice piece of nose-to-tail cooking. But 'potato salad' in Japan means mayonnaise, which is EGG, so not vegan; and it usually carries ham or bacon. Okara itself is soy pulp, not wheat — note this is the opposite of おからパン, which normally has wheat flour in it too. Ask about the binder and any ham.

items.en: Fresh wheat-gluten cake glazed with sweet miso and grilled
items.note: THE TRAP DISH ON THIS MENU. 麩 (fu) is PURE WHEAT GLUTEN — it is made by washing the starch out of wheat dough and keeping the gluten. It sits on a tofu menu, next to genuinely plant-based dishes, and it is about the most concentrated gluten you can eat. It is meanwhile perfectly plant-based, which is exactly what makes it dangerous: a vegan traveller's instinct and a coeliac's give opposite answers. Vegan filed `ask` only because dengaku miso is classically creamed with egg yolk and the miso may be barley.

items.en: Rolled dashi omelette
items.note: Egg — not vegan, and the dashi is bonito. On gluten: a Japanese kitchen builds dashimaki with 白だし or だし醤油, which are soy sauce and therefore WHEAT. Both diets fail on the same ingredient.

items.en: Chicken grilled with shichimi and sansho pepper — the shop uses 赤笹系軍鶏 jidori delivered direct from the producer
items.note: Chicken — not vegan. A yakitori-style grill is marinated or basted in a soy-sauce tare; wheat. Note also that commercial 七味唐辛子 blends sometimes include 麻の実 and other seeds but not usually wheat — the tare is the problem, not the spice.

items.ja: ずわい蟹の豆乳クリームコロッケ
items.en: Snow-crab croquette in a soy-milk cream
items.note: Crab — not vegan. A croquette is crumbed in PANKO and the cream filling is thickened with a roux, i.e. wheat twice, plus a shared fryer with the tempura station. Using soy milk instead of dairy does not make it either dairy-free-relevant or wheat-free.

items.ja: 海老しんじょうの湯葉包み揚げ
items.en: Prawn shinjo wrapped in yuba and deep-fried
items.note: Prawn — not vegan. しんじょう is a fish/prawn paste bound with egg white and usually 大和芋 and starch, but commercial shinjo commonly contains wheat starch, it is fried in the shared tempura oil, and it is served with a dashi-soy sauce.

items.en: Gyoza wrapped in yuba instead of dough
items.note: GENUINELY INTERESTING: the one gyoza in Tokyo whose wrapper is not wheat — yuba is soy-milk skin, so the usual 餃子の皮＝小麦 rule does not apply here. But the FILLING is almost certainly pork and is seasoned with soy sauce, and the dipping sauce is soy plus vinegar. So: not vegan, and gluten still needs confirming on the filling and the dip rather than the wrapper. Worth asking about — this is the sort of dish the rule of thumb gets wrong.

items.en: Rice with yuba under a thickened sauce
items.note: Rice and yuba are both clean; あんかけ is the problem — the thickened sauce is dashi (bonito) plus soy sauce, thickened with starch. Wheat from the soy, fish from the dashi.

items.en: Rice with tofu poured over it
items.note: ぶっかけ means poured over with tsuyu — めんつゆ or だし醤油, which is soy sauce (wheat) built on bonito dashi (not vegan). The rice and tofu underneath are fine; the liquid is not.

items.en: Tofu tiramisu
items.note: A tiramisu is built on SAVOIARDI sponge fingers — wheat — and there is no indication the shop replaces them. Using tofu in place of mascarpone may or may not make it plant-based; espresso, cocoa and tofu are fine but the sponge and any egg are not published. Ask.

items.ja: 豆乳のレアチーズケーキ
items.en: Soy-milk no-bake cheesecake
items.note: A レアチーズケーキ sits on a crushed-BISCUIT base — wheat — and it is set with GELATINE as standard, which is animal. Neither the biscuit nor the setting agent is displaced by using soy milk. Two hidden ingredients, neither of them in the name.

items.en: Assorted tempura — fried and served to the table as it comes out
items.note: Tempura batter is WHEAT flour and egg. The tentsuyu dip is dashi plus soy plus mirin. Everything in this section shares one fryer, so even the vegetable pieces below carry batter and cross-contact.

items.en: Large prawn tempura, per piece
items.note: Prawn — not vegan. Wheat batter.

items.en: Japanese whiting tempura, per piece
items.note: Fish — not vegan. Wheat batter.

items.en: Bamboo-shoot tempura, per piece
items.note: A SPRING item — bamboo shoot; unlikely to be on the board in late summer. The shoot is a plant but the batter is wheat and egg, and the fryer is shared with prawn and whiting.

items.en: New-potato tempura, per piece
items.note: A SPRING item. Wheat-and-egg batter, shared fryer with seafood.

items.en: Caprese tempura — tomato and mozzarella, battered
items.note: Mozzarella is dairy — not vegan. Wheat batter.

items.en: Angelica-tree shoot tempura, per piece — a classic spring sansai
items.note: A SPRING item. Wheat-and-egg batter, shared fryer.

items.ja: カマンベールチーズ（天ぷら）
items.en: Camembert tempura, per piece
items.note: Dairy — not vegan. Wheat batter.

items.en: New-onion tempura, per piece
items.note: A SPRING item. Wheat-and-egg batter, shared fryer with seafood.

tokyo_gazzo.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Taken from the shop's own グランドメニュー and ワイン・ドリンク pages on 2026-08-25. IMPORTANT: the page states 「※税別表記となります」 — every figure below EXCLUDES consumption tax, so add 10%. Address confirmed 千代田区三崎町2-2-15 大場ビル1F, 3 min from Suidobashi east exit. Lunch Mon–Fri 11:30–14:30, dinner Mon–Sat 18:00–22:00, closed Sun and holidays. The lunch page says only 「メニューはお店にてご覧ください」 (L.O. 14:00) — no lunch dishes are published, so none are listed here. A ピッツァ section (Margherita ¥1,450, octopus & pine-nut genovese ¥1,650, capricciosa ¥1,400〜) and an おつまみ section exist in the page source but are HTML-COMMENTED OUT, i.e. withdrawn from the live menu — they are deliberately not transcribed. The shop also runs a daily blackboard: 「内容は店内の黒板をご覧頂くか、スタッフまでお気軽にお尋ねください」. No allergen information is published anywhere on the site; every gf/vegan value below is reasoning from the dish name, not a shop statement, and a pasta kitchen means airborne flour throughout.

items.ja: 今日、食べて欲しい前菜3種盛り合わせ
items.en: Chef's three-item antipasto plate — composition changes daily
items.note: Contents change daily and are not published, so nothing can be said about it in advance — this is the one dish where you must ask before ordering. Assume a bread or crostino element unless told otherwise.

items.ja: 本日の鮮魚のカルパッチョ
items.en: Carpaccio of the day's fresh fish
items.note: Raw fish — not vegan. Italian carpaccio dressing is usually just oil, citrus and salt, but Japanese kitchens routinely reach for 醤油 or a soy-based ponzu in the mix, and Japanese soy sauce is wheat-brewed. Ask what is on it.

items.ja: 黒豚のパテドカンパーニュ
items.en: Country pâté of Kurobuta black pork
items.note: Pork — not vegan. Pâté de campagne is normally bound with breadcrumbs or flour and is served with bread; treat as wheat unless the kitchen says otherwise.

items.ja: 水牛モッツァレラのカプレーゼ
items.en: Caprese of buffalo mozzarella, tomato and basil
items.note: Buffalo mozzarella is dairy — not vegan. The dish itself carries no wheat ingredient, but this is a pasta and fritto kitchen with no allergen protocol, so it cannot be called safe; ask whether anything is dressed with balsamic glaze or served on bread.

items.ja: マグロとアボカドのタルタル　メルバトースト
items.romaji: maguro to avocado no tartare, melba toast
items.en: Tuna and avocado tartare with melba toast
items.note: Melba toast is wheat bread, served on the plate. Tuna — not vegan.

items.ja: ボロネーゼポテトサラダ
items.en: Potato salad topped with bolognese ragù
items.note: Meat ragù and mayonnaise (egg) — not vegan. Ragù is often let down with stock or thickened; ask. Wheat is not obvious here but is not excluded either.

items.en: Smoked mackerel
items.note: PRICE DELIBERATELY BLANK — the shop's own menu page has an empty price cell for this line while the neighbouring items are priced, so no figure is evidenced. Mackerel — not vegan. Smoked fish is frequently brined with soy sauce or mirin in a Japanese kitchen; ask.

items.ja: 生姜と季節野菜のピクルス
items.romaji: shōga to kisetsu yasai no pickles
items.en: Pickled ginger and seasonal vegetables
items.note: Vegetables in vinegar — the most likely plant-only plate on the card, but the pickling liquid is not published and Japanese pickling brines often include だし or honey. Ask; the answer is probably yes.

items.en: Smoked olives
items.note: Olives are a plant food and the dish carries no obvious wheat, but the marinade and any smoking seasoning are not published. A cheap, easy ask at the counter.

items.ja: 自家製クレイジーナッツ
items.en: House-spiced 'crazy' nuts
items.note: House-seasoned nuts. Spiced-nut mixes commonly use butter, honey or a soy-sauce glaze, any of which would change both answers, and the seasoning is not published. Contains tree nuts.

items.en: Prosciutto crudo
items.note: Cured pork — not vegan. Prosciutto itself is normally just pork and salt; the risk is what it is served with (bread, grissini) in a flour kitchen.

items.en: Cheese plate
items.note: Dairy — not vegan. Cheese boards arrive with crackers or bread as a matter of course; ask for it without.

items.en: 'Field' salad of ten vegetables — the shop uses organic, pesticide-free produce from contracted farms
items.note: The vegetables are fine; the dressing is the question, and it is not published. In Japan a house dressing is very often soy-sauce based (wheat) and/or contains egg or dashi. Ask for oil and vinegar and both answers usually become yes.

items.ja: ベーコンと温玉シーザーサラダ
items.en: Caesar salad with bacon and a soft-poached egg
items.note: Bacon, egg and a Caesar dressing built on cheese and anchovy — not vegan. Caesar salad carries croutons as standard and Caesar dressing routinely contains Worcestershire sauce, which is wheat.

items.en: The day's charcoal-grilled vegetables — direct from Yokoi Farm
items.note: Grilled vegetables with nothing else named — the most promising vegan candidate on the menu. Check the finishing seasoning (butter, anchovy and soy-based sauces are all common on a grill station) and note the grill is shared with meat.

items.ja: 生ウニとカマンベールのオーブン焼き
items.en: Oven-baked fresh sea urchin with Camembert
items.note: Sea urchin and cheese — not vegan. Price transcribed exactly as printed on the shop's page (¥350, tax excluded); it is far below its neighbours, so confirm it at the counter. Baked cheese dishes are usually finished on or with bread.

items.en: Today's ajillo — the day's ingredient simmered in garlic and olive oil
items.note: Ajillo is normally seafood, and it is served to be mopped up with bread, which is where the wheat arrives. The oil itself is usually clean; ask them to hold the baguette.

items.ja: お肉屋さんちの"おつまみ"ラビオリ
items.en: 'Butcher's snack' ravioli
items.note: Ravioli — the pasta wrapper is wheat. Meat filling; not vegan.

items.ja: ガーリックバターポテトフライ
items.en: Garlic-butter chips
items.note: Butter — not vegan. Deep-fried in the same fryer as the flour-coated カラマリフリット, so cross-contamination is a given even if the potatoes are unfloured.

items.ja: カラマリフリット　アイオリソース
items.en: Fried calamari with aioli
items.note: Fritto = wheat-flour coating. Squid and an egg-based aioli; not vegan.

items.ja: トリッパのアラビアータ
items.en: Tripe stewed in spicy tomato
items.note: Beef tripe — not vegan. Tomato and chilli carry no wheat in themselves, but tripe stews are often started with a floured roux or finished with bread; and it is served to be eaten with bread.

items.ja: 豚タンのコンフィ　グリーンペッパーとレモン
items.romaji: buta-tan no confit, green pepper to lemon
items.en: Confit of pork tongue with green peppercorns and lemon
items.note: Pork — not vegan. A confit is meat cooked in fat and carries no inherent wheat, but the cure and the finishing sauce are not published.

items.ja: 旬野菜のペペロンチーノ
items.en: Peperoncino with the season's vegetables
items.note: Durum wheat pasta — not gluten-free, and there is no GF pasta on this menu. Garlic, oil, chilli and vegetables is the one plausibly plant-only sauce here, but Japanese kitchens often add anchovy or a splash of stock to a peperoncino; ask.

items.ja: もちもちニョッキのゴルゴンゾーラクリーム
items.en: Chewy gnocchi in gorgonzola cream
items.note: Gnocchi is potato bound with wheat flour, and 「もちもち」 chewiness in particular comes from the flour. Gorgonzola and cream are dairy.

items.ja: あなたの言いなりパスタ
items.en: 'Whatever you say' pasta — tell the kitchen what you want and they build it
items.note: Wheat pasta, so gluten-free is not available however you specify it. But a made-to-order dish is the best vegan opening on the menu — the shop's line is 「上記メニュー以外にも…あなたの食べたいもの叶えます」. State no meat, fish, dairy, egg or anchovy explicitly.

items.ja: あなたの言いなりリゾット
items.en: 'Whatever you say' risotto — built to order
items.note: Rice, not pasta, and made to order — the single most negotiable dish on this menu for either diet. What decides it is the stock (usually chicken or fish), the finishing butter and cheese, and the fact that flour is airborne in this kitchen. Worth the conversation; do not assume.

items.en: New Zealand lamb, charcoal-grilled — 200 g
items.note: Lamb — not vegan. All three mains are stated ALL 200g. Plain grilled meat is usually wheat-free; the sauce is not published, and a Japanese-Italian grill sauce is frequently soy or balsamic-and-soy based.

items.en: Today's charcoal-grilled beef — 200 g
items.note: Beef — not vegan. Cut changes daily. Ask what the sauce is: soy-based grill sauces are wheat.

items.en: Today's charcoal-grilled pork — 200 g of the house 国産ブランド豚, killed that morning and delivered the same day
items.note: Pork — not vegan. This is the shop's signature ingredient; its year-round standard is 「国産ブランド豚の超低温ロースト」. Sauce not published; ask.

items.en: Rich chocolate gateau
items.note: Gateau chocolat is a flour, butter and egg cake. Not vegan, and treat as wheat.

items.en: Today's cheesecake
items.note: Cream cheese and egg — not vegan. A cheesecake base is a biscuit or sponge crumb, i.e. wheat.

items.en: Seasonal gelato
items.note: Gelato is a milk product — not vegan, and the flavour changes so it may carry biscuit or cookie pieces. Ask which flavour is on today and whether a wafer comes with it.

items.en: Wine by the glass — red, white, orange and sparkling all available
items.note: Grape wine is not a gluten grain, but the shop publishes nothing about fining agents, and wine is routinely fined with egg white, casein, gelatine or isinglass — that is the vegan question here. The owner's stated policy is cheap-but-good bottles from Italy, France, Spain, Australia, South Africa and Venezuela; staff will pick to your dish and budget.

items.ja: サッポロ 黒ラベル
items.en: Sapporo Black Label draught beer
items.note: Beer is brewed from BARLEY malt — a gluten grain, and never gluten-free.

items.ja: ヒューガルデン・ホワイト
items.en: Hoegaarden witbier
items.note: A witbier — barley malt AND unmalted WHEAT. Doubly disqualifying.

items.en: Today's guest beer
items.note: Beer — barley malt, gluten. Changes daily.

items.en: Highball, hard-carbonated
items.note: Whisky is distilled from malted BARLEY (and often other grains). Distillation removes most gluten protein but the app does not treat whisky or highballs as gluten-free.

items.ja: ノンアルコールビール
items.en: Alcohol-free beer
items.note: Alcohol-free beer is still brewed from barley malt — removing the alcohol does not remove the gluten.

items.en: Setouchi lemonade
items.note: Lemon and sugar syrup; no grain ingredient is implied, but the shop publishes no ingredient list and honey is a common lemonade sweetener.

items.en: Ginger ale
items.note: Despite the word 'ale' this is a soft drink, not a brewed beer. No ingredient list published.

items.en: Orange juice
items.note: Fruit juice; brand not published.

items.ja: グレープフルーツジュース
items.en: Grapefruit juice
items.note: Fruit juice; brand not published.

items.en: Oolong tea
items.note: Oolong is a true tea leaf, not a grain — unlike 麦茶, the barley tea served free in many Japanese restaurants, which is gluten. Brand not published.

items.ja: ソーダ / トニックウォーター
items.en: Soda water ¥440 / tonic water ¥440
items.note: Carbonated mixers. No grain ingredient implied; brand not published.

items.ja: カクテル（カシス／ピーチ／カンパリ／ウォッカ／ラム／ジン／梅酒ベース）
items.en: Cocktails to order — cassis, peach, Campari, vodka, rum, gin or umeshu base; the bar will build to your taste and strength
items.note: Cassis orange and Campari orange are listed at ¥680, moscow mule and screwdriver ¥680, gin & tonic ¥680; the ¥550〜 band covers the rock/water/soda/tonic/ginger/juice mixers. Vodka can be grain-distilled (Wilkinson, Smirnoff, Żubrówka are all on the shelf) and the app does not treat grain spirits as gluten-free; umeshu is usually shōchū-based and often contains honey.

items.ja: ウイスキー（シーバスリーガル12年／メイカーズマーク／グレンリベット12年／ラフロイグ10年／山崎）
items.en: Whisky — Chivas Regal 12, Maker's Mark, Glenlivet 12, Laphroaig 10, Yamazaki
items.note: All malt or grain whiskies — barley, and in Maker's Mark's case also wheat in the mash bill. Not treated as gluten-free here.

tokyo_uoshin_shinjuku.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Tax-included, from the Tabelog menu registration, 更新日 2026/08/21 — four days old at the time of checking, so this is current. The shop's own site (uoshins.com/shinjuku, operated by 株式会社シン) carries the address, hours and seating but publishes NO menu, so this is filed `partial` rather than `authoritative`. Address confirmed on both: 新宿区新宿3-35-5 2F, one minute from the JR Shinjuku southeast exit; 17:00–23:00 Mon–Sat, 16:00–23:00 Sun and holidays; 40 seats, all non-smoking. Two things the menu itself tells you: nearly every section is headed 「※一例です」 (this is a sample — the real list is the day's market), and the 「すぐ出ます。」 section is prefaced 「お通しが無いので。」 — this izakaya charges NO otoshi/table cover, which Tabelog's shop info confirms (お通し、チャージ料なし). Sashimi and grilled-fish items are day-priced and their price cells are empty on the shop's own registration; they are left empty here rather than guessed. No allergen information is published anywhere.

items.en: Assorted sashimi — the house signature, 「魚真と言えばコレです」. From two portions
items.note: Raw fish — not vegan. Price is per person, minimum two. Sashimi is eaten with 醤油, which in Japan is brewed with WHEAT; the fish itself is clean but the dip is not, and no tamari is offered. Bring your own GF soy sauce if this matters.

items.en: Horsehair crab — already picked out of the shell, 「ほぐしてあります。食べるだけ。」
items.note: PRICE NOT PUBLISHED — the shop's own registration leaves this cell blank because it is market-priced. Crab — not vegan. Plain steamed crab carries no wheat, but ask what it is served with; ponzu is usually soy-based.

items.en: 'Piled-on' sushi — negitoro, crab, salmon roe and sea urchin all on one bowl
items.note: Fish and roe — not vegan. Sushi rice is seasoned with vinegar and sugar (usually fine) but negitoro seasoning and the accompanying soy are wheat. Ikura is cured in soy sauce as standard.

items.en: Fresh (never-frozen) tuna sashimi
items.note: Day-priced; the shop's own list gives no figure. Raw fish — not vegan; wheat soy sauce is the dip. The whole 刺身 section is headed 「※一例です」 — what is on the board depends on that morning's market.

items.en: Beltfish / scabbardfish sashimi
items.note: Day-priced, no figure published. Raw fish; the soy dip is wheat.

items.en: Splendid alfonsino sashimi
items.note: Day-priced, no figure published. Raw fish; wheat soy sauce.

items.en: Common octopus sashimi
items.note: Day-priced, no figure published. Octopus; wheat soy sauce.

items.en: Golden cuttlefish sashimi
items.note: Day-priced, no figure published. Squid; wheat soy sauce.

items.en: Raw sweet prawn
items.note: Day-priced, no figure published. Prawn; wheat soy sauce.

items.en: Fresh sea urchin
items.note: Day-priced, no figure published. Sea urchin; wheat soy sauce. Note most commercially boxed uni is treated with alum, not a gluten issue but worth knowing.

items.en: Vinegar-cured mackerel
items.note: Day-priced, no figure published. Salt-and-vinegar cured mackerel; the cure itself is usually wheat-free but it is served with wheat soy sauce, and 昆布〆 versions sit on kelp seasoned with mirin.

items.en: Red sea bream sashimi
items.note: Day-priced, no figure published. Raw fish; wheat soy sauce.

items.en: Bonito sashimi / tataki
items.note: Day-priced, no figure published. Bonito is usually served tataki-style with a ponzu that is soy-based — wheat.

items.en: Scallop sashimi
items.note: Day-priced, no figure published. Scallop; wheat soy sauce.

items.en: Whelk sashimi
items.note: Day-priced, no figure published. Shellfish; wheat soy sauce.

items.en: Surf clam sashimi
items.note: Day-priced, no figure published. Shellfish; wheat soy sauce.

items.en: Blackthroat seaperch, grilled
items.note: Day-priced, no figure published. Fish — not vegan. A plain SALT-grilled fish (塩焼き) is one of the few genuinely wheat-free ways to eat in an izakaya; a 煮付け or 照り焼き is soy-simmered and is not. Ask which way it comes.

items.en: Herring, grilled
items.note: Day-priced, no figure published. Fish. Same question: salt-grilled is wheat-free, soy-simmered is not.

items.en: Kichiji rockfish, grilled or simmered
items.note: Day-priced, no figure published. Kinki is very often served 煮付け — simmered in soy sauce, mirin and sugar, which is wheat. Ask for 塩焼き if you need it clean.

items.en: Tilefish 'pine-cone' grill — the scales left on and fried crisp, 「うろこパリパリ。」
items.note: Day-priced, no figure published. Fish — not vegan. Matsukasa-yaki crisps the scales in hot oil rather than in batter, so the fish itself may be clean; the risk is a shared fryer with the tempura and kara-age, and any soy-based finishing sauce. Ask.

items.en: Norwegian mackerel, dried and grilled — 「ノルウェー人に感謝。」
items.note: Day-priced, no figure published. Fish. 文化干し is a salt-brine dry-cure, usually wheat-free, but it is served with grated daikon and soy sauce.

items.en: Salt-grilled beltfish
items.note: Day-priced, no figure published. Fish — not vegan. Explicitly 塩焼き, i.e. salt-grilled rather than soy-glazed, which makes it the most promising wheat-free cooked dish on the board. Ask only about the grill being shared and the accompanying dip.

items.en: Grilled fish collar and head — 「何があるかはその日次第。別紙にて。」 (whatever came in; on a separate sheet)
items.note: Priced on a separate slip in the shop, not published. Fish. Usually salt-grilled; ask about any glaze.

items.en: Fish marinated in sweet white miso and grilled — house-cured, on a separate sheet
items.note: Priced on a separate slip, not published. Fish — not vegan. Saikyo miso is a RICE-koji white miso, so it is not 麦味噌 (barley), but the marinade normally also carries mirin and sake and sometimes soy; and any Japanese miso is worth asking about because barley miso is common and barley is NOT on Japan's statutory allergen list.

items.en: Assorted tempura — three kinds, changing daily
items.note: Price not published. Tempura batter is WHEAT flour, and the tentsuyu dip is dashi plus soy sauce plus mirin — wheat again, and bonito dashi rules out vegan. The fryer is shared with everything else fried here.

items.en: Clams steamed in sake — local hamaguri and asari
items.note: Price not published. Shellfish — not vegan. Sake-steamed clams are often just sake, salt and clam liquor, which would be wheat-free; but many kitchens add butter or a splash of soy. Worth asking — this is a real candidate.

items.en: Grilled aubergine with the house sweet miso
items.note: Price not published. Aubergine and miso is the closest thing to a plant dish here, but 自家製玉味噌 (tamamiso) is classically miso creamed with EGG YOLK, sugar and mirin — so it is very likely not vegan, and the miso base may be barley. Ask specifically whether the tamamiso contains egg.

items.en: Chopped fatty tuna with pickled daikon, served without rice — roll it in the nori yourself
items.note: Tuna — not vegan. Torotaku is dressed with soy sauce as standard, and takuan pickle is often coloured and seasoned with a soy or amino-acid liquor. Wheat.

items.en: Lightly pickled zha cai (Sichuan mustard stem) — 「やみつきになります。」
items.note: A vegetable pickle, so plausible for both diets, but zha cai is normally dressed with sesame oil and often with soy sauce or oyster sauce. Ask.

items.en: Pufferfish skin in ponzu — 「美肌になりましょう。」
items.note: Fish skin — not vegan. Ponzu is citrus PLUS soy sauce plus dashi, so it is wheat and it is bonito. Ponzu is one of the most reliable hidden-wheat traps in an izakaya.

items.en: Lightly seared spicy cod roe — 「炙ればだいたい旨い。」
items.note: Fish roe — not vegan. Mentaiko is cured in a seasoning liquor built on soy sauce, mirin and sake; commercial mentaiko almost always declares 小麦.

items.en: Shark cartilage with pickled plum — 「すっぱコリコリ。」
items.note: Shark cartilage — not vegan. Umesuisho is dressed with soy sauce and mirin as standard.

items.en: Jellyfish in ponzu
items.note: Jellyfish — an animal, not vegan. Ponzu is soy-based: wheat, plus bonito dashi.

items.en: Fish trimmings simmered — ¥100, limited quantity, one per customer (「おかわりゴメンナサイ。」)
items.note: Fish — not vegan. 煮 means simmered in soy sauce, mirin and sugar. Wheat. Spectacular value at ¥100 but not for either diet.

items.en: Salmon roe sac with grated daikon — 「塩漬けなので少しずつ。」 salt-cured, so eat it slowly
items.note: Roe — not vegan. The shop explicitly says this one is SALT-cured (塩漬け) rather than the usual soy-cured, which is genuinely interesting for gluten; but it will arrive with soy sauce over the daikon. Ask them to hold it.

items.en: Akita smoked daikon pickle with mascarpone
items.note: Mascarpone is dairy — not vegan. いぶりがっこ is smoked, rice-bran-pickled daikon; the pickling bed is nuka (rice bran) and usually wheat-free, but commercial versions often add an amino-acid seasoning. Ask.

items.en: Mozuku seaweed in vinegar — 「海藻ファーストしましょう。」
items.note: Looks like the vegan option and is not. Bottled もずく酢 dressing is vinegar plus sugar plus 出汁 — bonito — and usually 醤油 as well, so it fails both tests at once. This is the classic 'seaweed salad is surely fine' trap.

items.en: Thick fried tofu, served hot and crisp
items.note: The tofu itself is soy and the fry coating is none — atsuage is fried bare. But it is served with 鰹節 (bonito flakes) and soy sauce as standard, which defeats vegan and adds wheat, and it comes out of the same fryer as the tempura. Ask for it plain and it becomes a real option.

items.en: Deep-fried fish bones — 「カルシウム食べましょう。」
items.note: Fish — not vegan. Fried, usually dusted with flour or potato starch, and in a shared fryer with the wheat-battered tempura.

items.en: Fried fishcake with onion
items.note: Fish paste — not vegan. Commercial satsuma-age is bound with starch and very commonly wheat flour, and it is eaten with soy sauce.

items.en: Fermented bonito viscera — 「酒好きへ。」 for the drinkers
items.note: Fermented fish guts — not vegan. Shuto is matured with sake, mirin and usually soy sauce; wheat.

items.en: Rolled omelette, generously dashi-soaked
items.note: Egg — not vegan, and the dashi is bonito. The shop's own line is 「お出汁たっぷり」, and a Japanese kitchen builds that dashi with 白だし or だし醤油, both of which are soy sauce and therefore WHEAT. Dashimaki looks innocent and is one of the most reliable wheat carriers on any izakaya menu.

items.en: Today's fish, fried then marinated in sweet vinegar
items.note: Fish — not vegan. Nanban-zuke is floured, fried, then steeped in a vinegar-soy-sugar marinade: wheat twice over.

items.en: Deep-fried octopus with ponzu
items.note: Octopus — not vegan. Kara-age coating plus soy-based ponzu; wheat in the coating, the marinade and the dip.

items.en: Fish-tube cake fried in seaweed batter — the shop says 「推してます。」
items.note: Fish paste — not vegan. 磯辺揚げ is a wheat-flour tempura batter with aonori in it; chikuwa itself usually contains wheat starch too.

items.en: Tuna in the style of chicken nanban — with tartare sauce
items.note: Tuna and an egg-mayonnaise tartare — not vegan. Nanban style means floured and fried then dipped in a sweet vinegar-soy sauce. Wheat.

items.en: Grilled eel-liver skewer
items.note: Eel liver — not vegan. Eel is glazed with tare, which is soy sauce, mirin and sugar. Wheat.

items.en: Deep-fried tofu in broth, with the day's fish
items.note: A tofu dish that is neither vegan nor gluten-free: the tofu is dusted in flour or starch and fried, the broth is bonito dashi plus soy sauce plus mirin, and it is topped with katsuobushi. The shop's version also has fish in it.

items.en: Salad heaped with boiled whitebait
items.note: Whitebait — not vegan. The dressing is the wheat question and is not published; Japanese house dressings are usually soy-based. Ask for oil and vinegar.

items.en: Fried aubergine steeped in broth — a long-running favourite
items.note: Vegetable, but 浸し means steeped in 出汁 — bonito dashi with soy sauce and mirin. Fails vegan on the dashi and gluten on the soy, and it is deep-fried in the shared fryer.

items.ja: おじゃがとキャベツのサラダ
items.en: Potato and cabbage salad — 「魚真と言えば。」 one of the two things the shop names as its own
items.note: Almost certainly mayonnaise-bound (egg) — not vegan. Dressing composition not published; ask about soy sauce.

items.en: Potato salad with the house-made tuna
items.note: House tuna and mayonnaise — not vegan. Wheat is not obvious but the mayonnaise and any seasoning are unpublished.

items.en: Raw 'water aubergine', sliced like sashimi — 「今だけ。」 in season now
items.note: Raw aubergine and nothing else — the single most plausible vegan plate on this menu. What decides it is the dip: it is normally served with soy sauce (wheat) or a dashi-shoyu (wheat and bonito). Ask for salt instead and both answers become yes.

items.en: Boiled edamame, 「茹でたて。」 fresh from the pot
items.note: Green soybeans boiled in salted water — no wheat, no animal ingredient in the dish as described. Filed `ask` rather than safe only because the shop publishes no allergen policy and the kitchen is full of soy sauce and shared water. In practice this is the reliable order here.

items.en: Red-hearted daikon with moromi miso and mayonnaise
items.note: Mayonnaise is egg — not vegan. もろみ味噌 is an unrefined moromi mash and is very commonly made with BARLEY (麦麹); barley is a gluten grain and is NOT on Japan's statutory allergen list, so it will not appear on any label. Treat as wheat/barley.

items.en: Tomato steeped in broth, with mizuna
items.note: お浸し means steeped in dashi — bonito, and the dashi is built on soy-based 白だし or めんつゆ. A vegetable dish that fails both tests on the liquid it sits in.

items.en: New-season burdock root, tatsuta-fried
items.note: 竜田揚げ means marinated in SOY SAUCE, mirin and sake, then coated in starch and fried — the soy marinade is the wheat, and it also defeats vegan if any dashi is in the marinade. Shared fryer with the fish.

items.en: Fried mountain yam glazed with dashi-soy
items.note: The shop's own description says 「出汁醤油をからめて」 — coated in DASHI-SOY. That single phrase answers both diets: soy sauce is wheat, bonito dashi is fish. Shared fryer as well.

items.en: Avocado with nori and wasabi
items.note: Avocado, seaweed and wasabi are all plant foods, which makes this a strong candidate. Two things to check: the dish is almost always dressed with soy sauce (wheat), and prepared wasabi paste routinely contains horseradish plus starch and sometimes wheat. Ask for it undressed.

items.en: Rice in broth — choose nori, pickled plum, mentaiko or salmon
items.note: The broth is dashi with soy sauce — wheat and bonito. The 明太子 and 鮭 fillings are fish; even the 梅 and 海苔 versions sit in the same soy broth.

items.en: Raw egg over rice, topped with crab
items.note: Raw egg and crab — not vegan. TKG is eaten with soy sauce, which is wheat.

items.en: Small whitebait rice bowl — 「ジャストサイズ。」
items.note: Whitebait — not vegan. Dressed with soy sauce; wheat.

items.en: Chopped seafood scattered over sushi rice — 「裏メニュー。」 an off-menu order
items.note: No price published — the shop itself calls it a 裏メニュー, an off-list item you have to ask for. Seafood — not vegan. Soy-marinated toppings and soy sauce; wheat.

items.en: Miso soup with aonori
items.note: Standard miso soup is bonito dashi — not vegan. On gluten: the miso itself may be 麦味噌, barley, which carries gluten and is not a labelled allergen in Japan, and the dashi is often a soy-based one. Ask what miso they use.

items.en: Fish-trimming soup — 「満足度満点。」
items.note: Fish — not vegan. Miso-based, so the same barley-miso question as the miso soup, plus the likelihood of a soy-based dashi.

items.en: Ice cream with brown-sugar syrup and roasted soy flour
items.note: Dairy ice cream — not vegan. Kuromitsu is cane syrup and kinako is roasted SOYBEAN flour, neither of which is a gluten grain; the unknowns are the ice-cream base and any wafer or biscuit served with it.

items.en: Seasonal sorbet — flavours on a separate sheet
items.note: Flavours are listed on a separate slip in the shop and are not published. A fruit sorbet is often dairy-free and wheat-free, which would make this the one dessert that works for both — but you must ask which flavour and whether it contains milk.

items.en: Thick-cut Unzen ham, crumbed and fried
items.note: Ham — not vegan. カツ means PANKO breadcrumb — wheat — and it comes out of the shared fryer. The sauce served with a katsu is Worcestershire-style, also wheat.

items.en: Fried chicken, salt-seasoned rather than soy — 「塩味です。」
items.note: Chicken — not vegan. The shop specifying 塩味 means the MARINADE is salt rather than soy sauce, which removes one wheat source and is genuinely unusual; but kara-age coating is flour or a flour-starch blend, and the fryer is shared with the wheat-battered tempura. Still no.
